9	# ADR-0002: Strapi access and security model
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	The browser must read published content (countries and form fields in US-01, plans in US-02,
14	terms in US-03) from Strapi, and nothing else. We must decide how the browser reaches Strapi
15	(directly or through a proxy, anonymously or with a token), how the same build learns the API
16	address in every environment, how we avoid caches that would hide a newly published change, and
17	how the AC-03 end-to-end test creates content without a write credential ever reaching the
18	browser (US-01-Q-23). Inputs: US-01-AC-27, US-01-AC-03, US-01-AC-13, US-01-BR-06, US-01-Q-16.
19	
20	## Decision Drivers
21	
22	- D1. "No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser. Public role permissions minimal and justified" (source: Assessment, security; CLAUDE.md §3). Evaluated as "token and permission security" (source: Assessment, evaluation).
23	- D2. "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-07). The build must not embed an environment-specific API address.
24	- D3. "Changing a form field or a plan in Strapi must be reflected in the app without changing code." (source: Assessment); visible on the next full page load, no cache delaying it (US-01-BR-06, US-01-Q-16).
25	- D4. "The whole project starts with a single command (for example docker compose up), with seed data for both countries" (source: Assessment, environment). Nothing may require a manual admin step to make the app work.
26	- D5. Drafts are never visible to end users (US-01-BR-06, US-01-AC-13).
27	- D6. AC-03 is automated: a test publishes a field during the run (US-01-Q-23), and the browser sees only GET requests without write tokens (US-01-AC-27).
28	- D7. Business editors use the Strapi admin, which must stay reachable (Assessment, business context).
29	
30	## Considered Options
31	
32	1. **Direct access with the public role**: the browser calls Strapi cross-origin with no token;
33	   the public role has `find`/`findOne` on the read types; the API URL comes from a runtime
34	   `config.json`.
35	2. **Same-origin nginx proxy + public role**: the nginx container that serves the Angular build
36	   forwards `GET /api/<allow-listed types>` to Strapi; the browser calls the relative path `/api`;
37	   Strapi's public role has only `find` on the read types and Strapi itself forces published
38	   content for anonymous requests.
39	3. **Same-origin nginx proxy injecting a read-only API token**: the public role has no content
40	   permissions; nginx adds `Authorization: Bearer <read token>` to proxied requests; the token
41	   lives only in the proxy's environment.
42	
43	## Decision Outcome
44	
45	Chosen option: **"2. Same-origin nginx proxy + public role"**, because it meets D1 with no token
46	anywhere near the browser and no secret to provision at start-up (D4), gives the same build a
47	relative API address that works in every environment (D2), and places the cache and method rules
48	in one small config file (D3, D6). The extra safeguard that matters most, forcing published
49	content, is enforced **inside Strapi**, so it holds even for requests that bypass the proxy (D5,
50	D7).
51	
52	### What is decided
53	
54	**Topology (docker compose)**
55	
56	- `frontend`: nginx (Docker Official Image) serving the Angular build on one origin, and proxying
57	  `/api/` to Strapi. The upstream address comes from an environment variable through the image's
58	  template mechanism (`/etc/nginx/templates/*.template` processed with `envsubst` into
59	  `/etc/nginx/conf.d` at container start; Docker Official Image "nginx" docs). The browser bundle
60	  contains no host name.
61	- `strapi`: exposes its own port for the admin panel used by editors (D7). The content API on that
62	  port is protected by the Strapi-side rules below, not by the proxy.
63	- Development (`ng serve`) uses the Angular dev-server proxy for `/api`, so the code path is the
64	  same relative URL. No `environment.ts` API URL, no runtime `config.json` (nothing to configure).
65	
66	**Proxy rules (nginx)**
67	
68	- Only `GET` (and the implicit `HEAD`) on an allow-list of paths: `/api/countries` and
69	  `/api/form-fields` in US-01; US-02 and US-03 add `/api/plans` and `/api/terms` through their
70	  specs. Any other method or path under `/api/` returns `405` or `404` without reaching Strapi.
71	- Responses under `/api/` carry `Cache-Control: no-store`; no `proxy_cache` is configured.
72	  `index.html` is served with `Cache-Control: no-cache`; hashed build assets may be cached long-term
73	  (their names change on every build).
74	- Requests carrying an `Authorization` header are rejected (`400`), so the proxy can never be used
75	  to replay a token from a browser.
76	
77	**Strapi rules (bootstrap code, idempotent, applied on every start; no manual admin clicks)**
78	
79	- Public role: **exactly** `api::country.country.find` and `api::form-field.form-field.find` in
80	  US-01 (US-02 adds `api::plan.plan.find`, US-03 `api::terms.terms.find`). No `findOne`: the app
81	  never reads a single document by `documentId`. Justification per permission is in the table
82	  below. Bootstrap reconciles the role to this list (removes anything else) on every start.
83	- The users-permissions defaults on the public role (`auth.callback`, `auth.connect`,
84	  `auth.forgotPassword`, `auth.resetPassword`, `auth.register`, `auth.emailConfirmation`,
85	  `auth.sendEmailConfirmation`, `auth.refresh`) are removed, and the advanced setting
86	  `allow_register` is set to `false`. Verified in `@strapi/plugin-users-permissions@5.63.0`:
87	  `services/users-permissions.js` (`DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS`) and `bootstrap/index.js`
88	  (`allow_register: true` by default). The app has no end-user accounts, so these endpoints are
89	  unneeded attack surface. Note: the plugin recreates its defaults only when the permissions table
90	  is empty (`syncPermissions`), which never happens while our `find` permissions exist.
91	- The authenticated role gets no content permissions.
92	- **Published only for anonymous reads.** The REST API accepts `status=draft` from any caller
93	  that has `find` (verified: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `content-api-constants.js` lists `status` as an
94	  allowed query parameter; `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `core-api/service/core-service.js` defaults it to
95	  `published` only when absent; the Strapi REST docs page on `status` states no permission
96	  requirement for `status=draft`). With a plain public `find`, anyone could read drafts with
97	  `?status=draft`. A Strapi global middleware therefore removes `status`, `publicationFilter` and
98	  `hasPublishedVersion` from content API requests that are not authenticated by an API token, so
99	  the default (`published`) always applies to anonymous reads.
100	- CORS (`strapi::cors`, default `origin: '*'` in `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `middlewares/cors.js`) is
101	  restricted to an environment-driven allow-list, empty by default: the browser reaches the
102	  content API same-origin through nginx and never needs CORS.
103	- Strapi creates a default "Full Access" API token on a fresh database with no admin user and no
104	  token (`@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `bootstrap.js`, `createDefaultAPITokensIfNeeded`). It never
105	  reaches the browser, but it is an unused write credential: bootstrap deletes the default
106	  "Full Access" token, and it is never copied into any `.env`.
107	
108	| Public permission | Why it is needed | Data exposed |
109	|---|---|---|
110	| `api::country.country.find` | Chooser, unknown-country links, currency and locale (ADR-0001); required by Strapi to filter `form-field` by `country.code` | Country code, name, currency, locale. Public by nature. |
111	| `api::form-field.form-field.find` | Step 1 form (US-01-BR-01) | Labels, rules, options, Spanish copy. Public by nature (shown to every visitor). |
112	
113	**Caching**
114	
115	- No HTTP cache interceptor and no service worker caching of `/api/` in Angular; content is loaded
116	  once per full page load and held in memory (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001).
117	- No Strapi REST cache plugin. Strapi 5.63.0 core sets no `Cache-Control` on content API
118	  responses (no occurrence in `@strapi/core@5.63.0/dist`); nginx adds `no-store`.
119	
120	**End-to-end writes for AC-03 (US-01-Q-23)**
121	
122	- The write credential exists only in the **Playwright Node process**. Flow:
123	  1. Bootstrap creates a development super admin from `STRAPI_ADMIN_EMAIL` /
124	     `STRAPI_ADMIN_PASSWORD` when no admin user exists (fictitious values in `.env.example`; real
125	     `.env` git-ignored). The human uses the same account at HC3.
126	  2. The test's setup logs in to the admin API (`POST /admin/login`, verified in
127	     `@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `routes/authentication.js`; the response includes an access token)
128	     directly against Strapi's port, not through nginx.
129	  3. It creates a **custom** API token (`POST /admin/api-tokens`, type `custom`, verified in
130	     `routes/api-tokens.js` and `services/constants.js`: types `read-only`, `full-access`,
131	     `custom`) scoped to `api::form-field.form-field.create` and `.delete`, with the shortest
132	     lifespan Strapi accepts (7 days; the validator accepts only `null`, 7, 30 or 90 days).
133	  4. It creates the `mobilePhone` field with `POST /api/form-fields` on Strapi's port. A REST
134	     `POST` publishes immediately unless `status=draft` is passed (Strapi REST docs, `status`
135	     page), which is what AC-03 needs.
136	  5. Teardown deletes the field and then the token (`DELETE /admin/api-tokens/:id`), also when the
137	     test fails.
138	- The token and the admin JWT are never passed to `page.evaluate`, `page.route`,
139	  `addInitScript`, cookies or storage of the browser context. The browser under test talks only to
140	  nginx, which rejects any `Authorization` header and any non-GET method.
141	
142	### Consequences
143	
144	- Good, because no token of any kind is ever sent by the browser or stored on disk by the app (D1).
145	- Good, because the same build runs in compose, in `ng serve` and in any future host: the API path
146	  is relative (D2).
147	- Good, because drafts stay unreadable even when someone calls Strapi's port directly with
148	  `?status=draft` (D5).
149	- Good, because one start command is enough: no token has to be generated and copied before the
150	  front end works (D4).
151	- Bad, because anyone who can reach Strapi's port can call the two public `find` endpoints
152	  directly, bypassing the proxy's allow-list — mitigation: the data is public by nature, drafts are
153	  blocked in Strapi, and the role has no other permission. Rate limiting is out of scope.
154	- Bad, because the published-only rule is custom middleware that a Strapi upgrade could make
155	  incomplete (for example a new publication query parameter) — mitigation: an automated check
156	  (below) requests the seeded draft field anonymously; re-verify on every Strapi upgrade.
157	- Bad, because the e2e setup depends on Strapi's admin API (`/admin/login`, `/admin/api-tokens`),
158	  which is what the admin panel uses but is less documented than the REST API — mitigation: it is
159	  used only by tests; if it changes, only the AC-03 test breaks, and the HC3 manual check of AC-03
160	  in the admin remains.
161	- Bad, because a development admin account is created from environment variables — mitigation:
162	  fictitious values only in `.env.example`, `.env` git-ignored, and `scripts/scan-secrets.sh`.
163	- Neutral: nginx is needed anyway to serve the Angular build; the proxy adds a few lines of
164	  configuration, not a new service.
165	
166	### Strongest argument against
167	
168	Strapi's own port, which stays open for the admin panel, still answers the public `find`
169	endpoints to anyone who can reach it, and those requests skip the proxy's method and path
170	allow-list entirely. On that port, keeping drafts hidden rests only on custom published-only
171	middleware, which a Strapi upgrade could quietly make incomplete (for example through a new
172	publication query parameter) without any error. Option 3 (proxy-injected read-only token, empty
173	public role) would close Strapi's port to anonymous content reads altogether.
174	
175	**Why we accept it:** the two exposed endpoints serve data that is public by nature, and the
176	public role has no other permission. Option 3 needs the token to exist before nginx starts,
177	which breaks the single start command (D4), and it gives the browser the same effective access
178	through the proxy, so its gain is limited to the direct port. The draft rule is guarded by an
179	automated anonymous request for the seeded draft field, re-run on every Strapi upgrade.
180	
181	### Confirmation
182	
183	- E2E `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27): every browser request to `/api/` is a `GET`, none has an
184	  `Authorization` header, none contains a step 1 value.
185	- Check in the same file (an API request from the Node process, no browser): anonymous
186	  `GET /api/form-fields?status=draft&filters[key][$eq]=email` on Strapi's port returns no `email`
187	  field; `POST /api/form-fields` through nginx returns `405`.
188	- E2E `us-01-config-change.spec.ts` (AC-03) follows the write flow above; review checks that the
189	  token is created and deleted in Node only.
190	- Review checklist: bootstrap reconciles the public role to the table above; `allow_register` is
191	  `false`; no `Authorization` header and no Strapi host name in `frontend/src`;
192	  `scripts/scan-secrets.sh` exits 0.
193	
194	## Pros and Cons of the Options
195	
196	### 1. Direct access with the public role
197	
198	- Good, because there is no proxy configuration at all.
199	- Bad, because the browser needs Strapi's absolute address, so the build needs a runtime
200	  `config.json` fetched before bootstrap (`provideAppInitializer`, present in
201	  `@angular/core@22.3.0`), a second artefact per environment.
202	- Bad, because Strapi's CORS (default `origin: '*'`) must be opened to the front-end origin.
203	- Bad, because caching and method rules can only live in Strapi.
204	
205	### 2. Same-origin nginx proxy + public role (chosen)
206	
207	- Good, because no token exists in the read path; nothing to provision.
208	- Good, because the API address is relative; CORS can be closed.
209	- Good, because method, path and cache rules sit in one reviewed file.
210	- Bad, because Strapi's own port still answers the public `find` endpoints (mitigated as above).
211	
212	### 3. Same-origin nginx proxy injecting a read-only API token
213	
214	- Good, because the public role can be empty: Strapi's port answers `403` to anonymous content
215	  requests.
216	- Bad, because the token must exist before nginx starts: Strapi generates the key randomly at
217	  creation (`@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `services/api-token.js`, `crypto.randomBytes`), so a single
218	  `docker compose up` would need Strapi to write the secret to a shared volume or to insert a
219	  pre-hashed key using its internal hashing, both fragile (D4).
220	- Bad, because the `read-only` type grants `find`/`findOne` on **every** content type, including
221	  future ones, and `status=draft` is still accepted; a `custom` token narrows it, but the
222	  published-only rule is still needed.
223	- Bad, because the proxy then grants anyone who reaches it the token's rights, so the browser's
224	  effective access is the same as option 2: the security gain is only on Strapi's direct port.
225	
226	## More Information
227	
228	- Verified sources (2026-11-20; packages fetched with `npm pack` into a temporary directory):
229	  `@strapi/core@5.63.0`, `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`, `@strapi/admin@5.63.0`,
230	  `@strapi/plugin-users-permissions@5.63.0`, `@angular/core@22.3.0` (files cited inline);
231	  https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/status (REST default `published`, `POST`/`PUT` publish
232	  unless `status=draft`); https://hub.docker.com/_/nginx (environment variables via templates).
233	- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (which types are per country, and why `country` must be readable),
234	  ADR-0003 (step 1 values never leave the browser).
235	- Revisit when: the app gains end-user accounts, content that is not public appears, Strapi's
236	  port must be reachable from the internet without the proxy, or Strapi adds a permission for
237	  reading drafts through the content API.

9	# ADR-0003: Front-end persistence of the wizard state
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	The wizard keeps the step 1 values (US-01), later the chosen plan (US-02), between steps and must
14	not send them to any server. The person must find their data when going back (US-01-AC-04,
15	US-01-AC-20) and, after a rejected payment, "try again without losing my information" (US-03
16	story). The values include personal data: the document number and the birth date. We must decide
17	where the state lives, what is stored, how it is scoped per country, and when it is cleared
18	(US-01-Q-15, answered "decided by the ADR; sessionStorage is the starting point", and
19	US-01-Q-02, default accepted).
20	
21	## Decision Drivers
22	
23	- D1. "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-08)
24	- D2. Data kept when going back, in-app and with browser back (US-01-AC-04, US-01-AC-20) and across a reload in the same tab, proposed by US-01-Q-15 (US-01-AC-21).
25	- D3. Data never crosses countries; opening another country's context discards the previous one (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22, US-01-Q-02).
26	- D4. Privacy: document number and birth date are personal data (US-01-Q-15; spec §9 security/privacy). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written to logs (US-01-AC-27, CLAUDE.md §3). Masking in the summary (US-03 story: "The document number is shown partially masked").
27	- D5. A changed configuration must not resurrect values of removed fields or options (US-01-Q-16, US-01-AC-23).
28	- D6. Retry after a failed payment keeps the data; a successful payment ends the quote (US-03 story: "Rejected payment", "Successful payment").
29	- D7. "Use fictitious data only." (source: Assessment). Tests and fixtures use only seed values.
30	
31	## Considered Options
32	
33	1. **In memory only** (a signal store, lost on reload).
34	2. **`sessionStorage`**, one versioned entry, scoped to one country, cleared on country change,
35	   tab close and successful payment.
36	3. **`localStorage` with an expiry** (for example 30 minutes), same shape.
37	4. **Hybrid**: `sessionStorage` for non-sensitive values, document number and birth date in
38	   memory only.
39	
40	## Decision Outcome
41	
42	Chosen option: **"2. sessionStorage"**, because it is the only option that survives a reload in
43	the same tab (D2) while being deleted by the browser when the tab closes, and its per-tab
44	partitioning keeps a CO tab and a CL tab from overwriting each other (D3). The privacy cost
45	(personal data in clear text in the tab's storage) is bounded by the tab lifetime and the
46	clearing rules below (D4).
47	
48	### What is decided
49	
50	**Store and storage key**
51	
52	- A root-provided `QuoteStore` (signals) is the single owner of the wizard state. Components and
53	  guards never touch `sessionStorage` directly.
54	- One `sessionStorage` entry, key `quote-wizard`, value JSON:
55	  `{ "version": 1, "country": "<code>", "step1": { "values": { "<key>": <value> } }, "plan": … }`.
56	  `values` holds the **raw editing values** of the form model: strings for `text`, `number`,
57	  `select` and `date`, booleans for `checkbox`, and `''` for an empty field. An in-progress
58	  invalid value such as `'2015.5'` is stored as typed. The spec §7.3 typed output (`text` →
59	  trimmed string, `number` → integer, `select` → option value, `date` → `YYYY-MM-DD`, `checkbox`
60	  → boolean, unchecked optional checkbox → `false`, empty optional → `null`) is produced only on a
61	  valid "Continuar"; that typed output is what US-02 and US-03 consume. `plan` is added by US-02
62	  (an identifier of the chosen plan only, defined in its spec).
63	- **Not stored**: the field configuration, labels, option labels, plans, prices or terms. They are
64	  fetched once per full page load (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001) and later steps read labels from that
65	  in-memory configuration. This settles the open point in spec §7.3 ("Whether it is stored or
66	  refetched is a persistence ADR detail"): refetched.
67	- **Never written to storage**: payment data (US-03), if the simulated payment asks for any. It
68	  lives only in the payment component's memory.
69	- No cookies, no `localStorage`, no IndexedDB for wizard data.
70	
71	**When it is written**
72	
73	- On every change of a step 1 value, the raw editing values are written (the store writes
74	  synchronously after updating its signal), so a reload restores exactly what the person typed,
75	  valid or not. The values are revalidated when shown and on "Continuar" (US-01-Q-16); only a
76	  valid "Continuar" produces the §7.3 typed output.
77	
78	**When it is read**
79	
80	- Once, when the store is created (each full page load). The JSON is validated at the boundary:
81	  wrong `version`, invalid JSON, a `country` that is not an alpha-2 code, or values of an
82	  unexpected type → the entry is discarded and a `console.warn` without any value is logged.
83	- When step 1 renders with the configuration of this page load: values whose key is no longer
84	  configured are dropped from the state, and a `select` value whose option no longer exists is
85	  cleared (US-01-AC-23). The pruned state is written back.
86	
87	**Scope per country (US-01-Q-02)**
88	
89	- The entry holds at most **one** country. When a supported country's context is entered
90	  (ADR-0001, `/:country` route) and the stored `country` differs, the entry is deleted before
91	  step 1 renders. Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not delete it.
92	- `sessionStorage` is partitioned by origin and by tab (MDN: "partitioned by both origin and
93	  browser tabs (top-level browsing contexts)"), so two tabs with different countries have
94	  independent state.
95	
96	**When it is cleared**
97	
98	| Event | Effect | Owner |
99	|---|---|---|
100	| Tab or window closed | Browser deletes it (MDN: "Closing the tab/window ends the session and clears the data in `sessionStorage`.") | Browser |
101	| Another supported country's context entered | Entry deleted | US-01 (`QuoteStore`, called from the `/:country` route) |
102	| Successful payment | Entry deleted before the confirmation is shown; the confirmation keeps only the simulated quote number in memory | US-03 |
103	| Rejected payment | **Nothing** cleared: the person retries with the same data | US-03 |
104	| Unreadable or wrong-version entry | Entry deleted | US-01 |
105	
106	**Privacy rules**
107	
108	- Values are never logged (no `console.*` with values, warnings name keys only), never sent in a
109	  request (US-01-AC-27), never put in the URL, and never in the document title.
110	- The full document number is stored, because US-03 masks it **at display time**; the masked form
111	  is never stored separately.
112	- No client-side encryption: the key would live in the same JavaScript as the data, so it would
113	  add complexity without protecting against the realistic threat (script injection in the page).
114	  The protection is the tab lifetime, the clearing rules and the absence of third-party scripts.
115	- If `sessionStorage` is unavailable (blocked by the browser, quota exceeded), the store keeps the
116	  state in memory only and logs one `console.warn`; the wizard still works except across reloads.
117	
118	### Consequences
119	
120	- Good, because the person keeps their data across steps, browser back and a reload (D2), and
121	  after a rejected payment (D6).
122	- Good, because the data disappears with the tab, with a country switch and after payment (D3, D4).
123	- Good, because one entry with a version number and boundary validation makes later stories'
124	  additions (plan) and format changes safe.
125	- Bad, because the document number and birth date sit in clear text in the tab's storage while
126	  the tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin and by anyone using the same
127	  browser tab — mitigation: no third-party scripts, values never logged, cleared on payment and
128	  country switch; the residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
129	- Bad, because MDN notes the page session "survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser
130	  that restores a crashed or reopened session may bring the data back — mitigation: accepted;
131	  the data stays on the same device and profile.
132	- Bad, because a tab opened from the wizard tab may start with a copy of its storage (MDN: with an
133	  `opener`, "the `sessionStorage` is initially a copy of the opener's") — mitigation: the app opens
134	  no new windows; copies are independent afterwards.
135	- Bad, because writing on every change stores invalid intermediate values — mitigation: they are
136	  revalidated on display and on "Continuar"; the AC-19 guard validates before step 2.
137	- Neutral: spec US-01-AC-21 ("Data survives a reload") stays as written; the "memory only"
138	  rewrite foreseen in the spec does not apply.
139	
140	### Strongest argument against
141	
142	The document number and birth date stay in clear text in the tab's storage for as long as the
143	tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin. MDN states that the page session
144	"survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser that restores a crashed or reopened
145	session can bring that personal data back. Option 1 (memory only) avoids all of this: nothing
146	personal is ever written to the device. Its only cost is that a reload loses the data.
147	
148	**Why we accept it:** losing everything on a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors,
149	fails the reload behaviour approved for AC-21 (D2), and the AC-19 guard would send the person
150	back to an empty step 1. The exposure is limited: no third-party scripts, values are never
151	logged, the entry is cleared on payment and on country switch, and the data stays on the same
152	device and browser profile. The residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
153	
154	### Confirmation
155	
156	- Unit tests `quote-store.spec.ts`: the raw editing values (including an in-progress invalid
157	  value such as `'2015.5'`) are persisted on every change, and a new store instance restores them
158	  exactly from `sessionStorage` (AC-21); the §7.3 typed output (AC-18) is produced only on a valid
159	  "Continuar", never on an invalid one; entering another country deletes the entry and the original
160	  country is empty afterwards (AC-22); removed keys and options are pruned (AC-23); a corrupted or
161	  wrong-version entry is discarded with a warning that contains no value; storage unavailable →
162	  memory fallback.
163	- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts` (AC-22) and `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27, no value in any
164	  request).
165	- Review checklist: only `QuoteStore` references `sessionStorage`; no `localStorage`, cookies or
166	  IndexedDB for wizard data; no `console.*` call receives a value; US-03 clears the entry on
167	  successful payment and not on a rejected one.
168	
169	## Pros and Cons of the Options
170	
171	### 1. In memory only
172	
173	- Good, because nothing is written to the device; the strongest privacy option.
174	- Good, because it is the simplest to implement and test.
175	- Bad, because a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors, loses everything (fails the
176	  reload behaviour proposed in US-01-Q-15; AC-21 would be rewritten).
177	- Bad, because a reload on step 2 or 3 sends the person back to an empty step 1 through the AC-19
178	  guard.
179	
180	### 2. `sessionStorage` (chosen)
181	
182	- Good, because it survives reloads and is cleared by the browser when the tab closes.
183	- Good, because it is partitioned per tab, so different countries in different tabs do not clash.
184	- Bad, because personal data is in clear text while the tab is open.
185	- Bad, because browser session restore can bring it back.
186	
187	### 3. `localStorage` with an expiry
188	
189	- Good, because the person could close the tab and come back within the expiry.
190	- Bad, because the data outlives the tab, so on a shared computer the next person can see it; the
191	  expiry is only enforced when the app runs again.
192	- Bad, because `localStorage` is shared by all tabs of the origin: a CO tab and a CL tab would
193	  overwrite each other's state.
194	
195	### 4. Hybrid (sensitive values in memory only)
196	
197	- Good, because the document number and birth date never touch storage.
198	- Bad, because after a reload the person must re-enter exactly the most tedious fields, and the
199	  AC-19 guard sends them back to step 1 with a partially filled form; AC-21 would hold only for
200	  some fields.
201	- Bad, because which keys are sensitive is decided in code, while editors can add new fields
202	  (for example a phone number) that would silently be stored.
203	
204	## More Information
205	
206	- MDN Web Docs, `Window.sessionStorage`
207	  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/sessionStorage), read on 2026-11-20:
208	  lifetime ("survives over page reloads and restores"; "Closing the tab/window ends the session
209	  and clears the data"), partitioning by origin and tab, copy from an opener.
210	- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (country context and the `/:country` route that triggers the switch),
211	  ADR-0002 (step 1 values never sent; AC-27), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved: how the form is
212	  hydrated from the store).
213	- Revisit when: the product needs to resume a quote on another day or device (that needs a
214	  server, out of scope), or real personal data is processed (a privacy review would then be
215	  required).
216	- Clarified at HC2 (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20): raw editing values in storage; §7.3 typed output
217	  only on a valid Continuar.

9	# ADR-0004: Forms library for the Strapi-driven step 1 form
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	Step 1 of the wizard (US-01) is a form whose fields, order, options, rules and Spanish copy all
14	come from Strapi at runtime (`specs/US-01/spec.md` §7.1, BR-01, BR-06). The field set is only
15	known after the configuration is fetched, so the form model is built at runtime. `CLAUDE.md` §7
16	blocks production form code until an ADR picks the forms approach, and `CLAUDE.md` §5 says the
17	vendored `angular-developer` skill's "You MUST use Angular's new Signal Forms API" is not
18	binding. SPIKE-01 built the same form twice, with Signal Forms and with Reactive Forms
19	(`FormRecord`), over a shared library-agnostic validation core. This ADR decides which approach
20	the production step 1 uses, and which parts stay outside the library.
21	
22	## Decision Drivers
23	
24	- **D1. Dynamic form with typed validations.** "Step 1 form generated dynamically from the
25	  Strapi configuration, with typed validations" (assessment); spec §9 *Typed validations*
26	  (configuration parsed at the boundary into a typed model; validators are pure functions with an
27	  injectable clock).
28	- **D2. Angular 21+ idioms.** "Angular 21 or later: standalone components, signals, built-in
29	  control flow (@if, @for), no NgModules" (assessment). Angular is pinned to **22.3.0**
30	  (`CLAUDE.md` §4).
31	- **D3. Error visibility and focus.** Errors appear after blur or after a failed "Continuar",
32	  update while typing once shown, and focus moves to the first invalid field in `sortOrder`
33	  (US-01-AC-10, US-01-Q-13).
34	- **D4. Hydration and pruning.** The form shows stored values on entry with no errors
35	  (US-01-AC-04, AC-20, AC-21); values of keys no longer configured are dropped and stale select
36	  values cleared (US-01-AC-23, Q-16).
37	- **D5. Correct empty and number semantics.** Required vs empty (`0` is a value, `''` is empty),
38	  integer-only numbers (US-01-AC-05, AC-08, Q-12, Q-26).
39	- **D6. Output shape.** Step 1 hands values to later steps in the §7.3 shape: trimmed text,
40	  integers, ISO dates, booleans, and `null` for an empty optional field.
41	- **D7. Accessibility.** Native controls, accessible name, description, required and invalid
42	  states, error announced once (US-01-AC-25, spec §9).
43	- **D8. Risk and reversibility.** Library maturity, amount of custom code, and the cost of
44	  switching later (`adr-madr`: hard-to-reverse decisions).
45	
46	## Considered Options
47	
48	1. **Signal Forms** (`@angular/forms/signals`: `form`, `FormField`, `FormRoot`, `validate`,
49	   `submit`) over the shared validation core.
50	2. **Reactive Forms** (`FormRecord<FormControl<…>>` with `ReactiveFormsModule`) over the same
51	   core.
52	3. **No forms library**: native inputs bound to plain signals (`[value]` / `(input)` /
53	   `(blur)`), with validation, touched state, submit and focus handled by the shared core and the
54	   component.
55	
56	## Decision Outcome
57	
58	Chosen option: **"Signal Forms over the shared validation core"**. Both libraries met every
59	SPIKE-01 criterion (11/11 each). The tie-breakers are D2, D3 and D5. Signal Forms keeps state in
60	signals with no bridges. `submit()` touches every field and `focusBoundControl()` moves focus
61	(D3), so neither needs a DOM lookup or an extra call. With a string model, number inputs had no
62	accessor surprises (D5). The Reactive Forms adapter needed `normalise()` to fix a real
63	functional bug: `NumberValueAccessor` wrote a number into a control declared as string, and a
64	valid year was read as empty. Its one typing advantage (no casts in templates) does not help D1,
65	because the typed contract lives in the parsed `FieldConfig` and the pure validators, not in
66	the form model.
67	
68	### What is decided
69	
70	- **Library and version:** `@angular/forms/signals` from `@angular/forms` 22.3.0 (pinned, as all
71	  `@angular/*`, by `CLAUDE.md` §4). The step 1 page does not import `ReactiveFormsModule`,
72	  `FormControl`, `FormGroup`, `FormRecord` or `@angular/forms/signals-compat`.
73	- **Validation stays in the core, not in the library.** Validation and message resolution are
74	  pure functions in `field-validators.ts` (`CLAUDE.md` §6). They import nothing from
75	  `@angular/forms` and get "today" from the injectable clock (US-01-Q-06). Each field gets
76	  exactly one `validate()` that calls the shared function and returns
77	  `{ kind: 'custom', message }`. Signal Forms built-in validators (`required()`, `min()`,
78	  `pattern()`, …) are not used. The rule order, the empty-optional skip (Q-26) and the message
79	  priority (Q-04) are configuration semantics, and keeping them in one function keeps this
80	  decision reversible (D8).
81	- **Editing model:** `Record<string, string | boolean>`. `text`, `number`, `select` and `date`
82	  hold strings (`''` = empty); `checkbox` holds a boolean. The model never holds `null`. This
83	  deliberately differs from the vendored skill's "use `0` for numbers": `0` is a valid value, so
84	  it cannot mean empty (D5, AC-08). `number` fields use a native `<input type="number">` bound to
85	  the string model, and integer-only is a validator rule (Q-12).
86	- **Output mapping:** the §7.3 values come from a pure `toOutput(configs, model)`: trimmed text,
87	  integer, option value, ISO date, boolean, and `null` for an empty optional field. The output is
88	  never read back into the form model; hydration goes through `hydrate()`.
89	- **Hydration and pruning:** the model is created from `hydrate(configs, storedValues)`, which
90	  keeps only configured keys and converts stored values to the editing model, **before** `form()`
91	  is called. Signal Forms does not drop unknown keys by itself (SPIKE-01 row g). Clearing a stale
92	  select value and writing the pruned state back belong to the store (ADR-0003).
93	- **Lifecycle:** the form is built once per configuration load, in the injection context of the
94	  component that owns it (a field initialiser of a form component created when the configuration
95	  is ready). `form()` is not called inside `computed()`, because it creates an effect
96	  (`NG0602`). A different configuration (another country) means a new component instance, not a
97	  rebuilt form inside a live one.
98	- **Error visibility:** an error is shown when `touched() && invalid()`, and only the first
99	  message (the core already resolves one message per field). "Continuar" calls `submit()` (or
100	  uses `FormRoot` with `submission` options). `submit()` marks every field as touched.
101	- **Focus on a failed attempt:** in `onInvalid`, focus the first invalid field in the
102	  configuration's `sortOrder` with `focusBoundControl()`.
103	- **Typing at the template boundary:** the runtime union `string | boolean` does not compile
104	  against native controls (SPIKE-01, *Typing*). Two narrowing accessors (`FieldTree<string>`
105	  and `FieldTree<boolean>`), selected by the field `type` in a static `@switch`, are the only
106	  casts allowed. They live in the step 1 form component and nowhere else.
107	- **Accessibility attributes** (`aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-required`, error
108	  element) are bound explicitly in the template, as in the spike. `provideSignalFormsConfig` is
109	  not relied on unless a later review shows it covers AC-25.
110	
111	### Consequences
112	
113	- Good, because the form state is signals end to end (D2): `valid()`, `touched()`, `errors()`
114	  feed the template and the wizard store with no `toSignal` or `valueChanges` bridges.
115	- Good, because blur and failed-submit visibility share one condition, and focus uses a library
116	  API instead of DOM queries by id (D3). The spike's sensitivity check proves the test catches its
117	  removal.
118	- Good, because the string editing model avoids the accessor writing `number | null` into a
119	  string-typed state (D5). Integer-only and required-vs-empty stay explicit, testable rules.
120	- Good, because the validation core is library-agnostic (209 lines in the spike) and is
121	  unit-tested without Angular forms. Switching library later means rewriting one adapter of
122	  about 110 lines plus its template, not the rules (D8).
123	- Bad, because Signal Forms has been public API only since **22.0.0 (2026-06-03)**, about five
124	  and a half months, and the `forms` scope has had **39** fix, perf or feat entries between
125	  22.0.0 and 22.3.0 in the CHANGELOG. Mitigation: pinned 22.3.0; the parts we use are small
126	  (`form`, `validate`, `submit`, `FormField`, `FormRoot`, `focusBoundControl`), all
127	  `@publicApi 22.0`; no async validators, no `debounce`, no `hidden`/`disabled` logic; validation
128	  semantics live outside the library.
129	- Bad, because the runtime model loses static typing in templates and needs two casts. A cast
130	  cannot catch a mismatch between a field's `type` and the accessor used. Mitigation: the
131	  accessor is picked in the same `@switch` branch that renders the control; a component test
132	  renders every field type and asserts the DOM value, and the review checklist rejects other
133	  casts on form fields.
134	- Bad, because an unknown key on the field tree compiles but throws at runtime
135	  (`TypeError: f.<key> is not a function`). Mitigation: the template iterates only over the
136	  parsed configuration, from which the model is built; no code indexes the tree by a literal key.
137	- Bad, because all SPIKE-01 evidence comes from jsdom: real focus, native date and number UI,
138	  `badInput` and screen reader announcements are unverified. Under the HTML value sanitisation
139	  rule for `type=number`, unparseable input such as `1e` makes `element.value` `''`, so it
140	  would show the "required" message rather than the format message. The spike did not exercise
141	  this. Mitigation: the CO e2e (US-01-T-11) exercises keyboard and
142	  validation in a real browser; the HC3 manual pass includes a screen reader check (spec §9).
143	- Neutral: Reactive Forms remains fully supported in 22.3.0 (`FormRecord` and
144	  `ReactiveFormsModule` are `@publicApi`, not deprecated). Later stories may revisit if a form
145	  needs something Signal Forms lacks.
146	
147	### Strongest argument against
148	
149	Signal Forms has been public API only since 22.0.0, about five and a half months, with 39
150	forms-scope fix, perf or feat entries through 22.3.0. All SPIKE-01 evidence comes from jsdom, not
151	a real browser. For a form built at runtime its typing benefit largely disappears: the template
152	needed casts, and an unknown key compiles but throws at runtime. Reactive Forms `FormRecord` is
153	the long-established path for runtime-keyed forms; in the spike it compiled with no casts, and
154	`setValue` throws on stale keys.
155	
156	**Why we accept it:** only APIs tagged `@publicApi 22.0` are used, with no async validators,
157	`debounce` or `hidden`/`disabled` logic, on a pinned 22.3.0. Validation semantics live outside
158	the library, so switching to Reactive Forms means rewriting one adapter of about 110 lines plus
159	its template, not the rules (D8). The Reactive adapter was not free of risk either: it needed
160	`normalise()` to fix a real bug where `NumberValueAccessor` wrote `number | null` into a
161	string-typed control (D5). The real-browser gap is covered by the CO e2e (US-01-T-11) and the
162	HC3 screen reader check.
163	
164	### Confirmation
165	
166	- **Tests (test-engineer, step 3):** component tests in `quote-form-page.spec.ts` for
167	  US-01-AC-10 (no errors on entry; error after blur; all errors and focus on the first invalid
168	  field in `sortOrder` after a failed "Continuar", checked through `document.activeElement`),
169	  US-01-AC-04 / AC-23 (hydrated values shown, pristine, stale key dropped, stale select shows the
170	  prompt) and US-01-AC-05 (`2015.5` invalid). Unit tests of `toOutput` for every §7.3 mapping.
171	- **Static checks (code-reviewer, step 6):**
172	  `grep -rnE "ReactiveFormsModule|FormControl|FormGroup|FormRecord|signals-compat" frontend/src/app`
173	  returns nothing. `field-validators.ts` imports nothing from `@angular/forms`. `form(` does not
174	  appear inside a `computed(`. The only `as unknown as FieldTree` casts are the two accessors.
175	- **Version:** `frontend/package.json` pins `@angular/forms` to exactly `22.3.0`.
176	
177	## Pros and Cons of the Options
178	
179	### 1. Signal Forms over the shared validation core
180	
181	SPIKE-01 adapter: `signal-forms/dynamic-form-signal.ts` + `.html` (111 lines).
182	
183	- Good, because it is the signal-native forms API, and Angular's own guide says "Signal Forms
184	  work best in new applications built with signals" (angular.dev Signal Forms overview, read
185	  2026-11-20). That matches D2.
186	- Good, because `submit()` touches the whole tree (verified in `@angular/forms@22.3.0`
187	  `fesm2022/_validation_errors-chunk.mjs`, `submit` calls `node.markAsTouched()`), and
188	  `FieldState.focusBoundControl()` is public API. Together they cover D3 with no custom
189	  plumbing (SPIKE-01 rows h, i).
190	- Good, because a string model on number and date inputs reads `element.value` with no
191	  conversion. Required-vs-empty and integer-only worked with no workaround (row a).
192	- Good, because hydration is "build the model, then the form", and the output maps cleanly to
193	  §7.3 with a non-null model (rows f, j; D4, D6).
194	- Bad, because it has been public for about 5.5 months, with steady fixes in 22.x (see
195	  *Consequences*).
196	- Bad, because the runtime union does not compile against native controls, so two casts are
197	  needed (row e).
198	- Bad, because `form()` creates an effect: it needs an injection context and cannot run inside
199	  `computed()` (`NG0602`).
200	- Bad, because the model does not prune unknown keys. Pruning must happen before the model is
201	  built (row g).
202	
203	### 2. Reactive Forms (`FormRecord`) over the shared validation core
204	
205	SPIKE-01 adapter: `reactive-forms/dynamic-form-reactive.ts` + `.html` (112 lines).
206	
207	- Good, because `FormRecord` is the long-established, documented path for forms keyed at
208	  runtime, and it is fully supported and not deprecated in 22.3.0 (`@publicApi` in
209	  `types/forms.d.ts`).
210	- Good, because `[formControl]` accepts `FormControl<string | boolean>` with **no casts**, and
211	  `controls[key]` / `get(key)` give an honest `undefined` / `null` for unknown keys (row e).
212	- Good, because `FormGroup.setValue` throws on extra keys, a built-in guard against stale
213	  stored keys (row g).
214	- Good, because it works with standalone components (`ReactiveFormsModule` is imported into the
215	  component; we write no NgModule), so D2's "no NgModules" is met.
216	- Bad, because `NumberValueAccessor` writes `number | null` into a control declared as
217	  `string | boolean`, and `nonNullable` does not prevent it. In the spike this made a valid year
218	  read as empty until `normalise()` was added to both the validator input and the output mapping
219	  (row a; D5). The declared type misdescribes the runtime value.
220	- Bad, because a failed submit touches nothing unless `markAllAsTouched()` is called, and there
221	  is no focus API, so focus needs a DOM lookup by id (rows h, i; D3).
222	- Bad, because control state (`touched`, `valid`) is not signals. A signals-based wizard needs
223	  bridges, or relies on template events to re-render under zoneless change detection (D2).
224	
225	### 3. No forms library: native inputs bound to plain signals
226	
227	Not built in SPIKE-01. Assessed from the shared core, which already does all parsing,
228	validation, hydration and output mapping without any forms API.
229	
230	- Good, because there is no adapter mismatch at all: each input binds `[value]` to a
231	  `string`/`boolean` signal and writes `element.value` / `element.checked` back. There are no
232	  casts and no value accessors.
233	- Good, because it has the smallest dependency surface. Nothing changes if a forms API changes
234	  in a later Angular release (D8).
235	- Good, because every behaviour (touched-on-blur, show-all-on-submit, focus) is explicit code
236	  that the tests read directly.
237	- Bad, because it re-implements what both libraries already provide: per-field touched state,
238	  submit handling, invalid aggregation, and focus by DOM lookup. That is more custom code to
239	  test and review (D3, D8).
240	- Bad, because there is no spike evidence for it. Its D3/D7 behaviour would be unproven until
241	  the production tests run.
242	- Bad, because a hand-rolled form in an assessment that grades "technical quality" on
243	  Angular 21+ idioms is a weaker signal than using the framework's forms API (D2).
244	
245	## More Information
246	
247	- **Spike:** [docs/spikes/SPIKE-01-forms.md](../docs/spikes/SPIKE-01-forms.md). Code on branch
248	  `spike/01-forms`, commit `be9ae50` (never merged):
249	  <https://github.com/FelipeSuarez25/multicountry-car-insurance/tree/spike/01-forms/spikes/spike-01-forms>.
250	  38/38 tests passed, re-run independently by the orchestrator with `@angular/core` and
251	  `@angular/forms` 22.3.0.
252	- **Verified facts (2026-11-20):**
253	  - npm `@angular/forms` dist-tag `latest` = `22.3.0`, published 2026-11-18; `22.0.0` published
254	    2026-06-03 (`npm view @angular/forms time`).
255	  - angular/angular `CHANGELOG.md`, release **22.0.0 (2026-06-03)**, forms: commit
256	    [`7745365910`](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/7745365910771d97c91e9b640c2c26a99bfa5a6d)
257	    "graduate signal forms APIs to public API". It matches EVAL-001, criterion 5
258	    (`docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md`).
259	  - Published `@angular/forms@22.3.0` typings (`npm pack` into a temp dir): `form`, `submit`,
260	    `FormField`, `FormRoot`, `validate`, `FieldState` (which declares `focusBoundControl`),
261	    `FormSubmitOptions` (`onInvalid`, `ignoreValidators`) and `provideSignalFormsConfig` are
262	    tagged `@publicApi 22.0`. The `@experimental` items are WebMCP-related
263	    (`experimentalWebMcpTool`, `provideExperimentalWebMcpForms`), which we do not use.
264	    `FormRecord`, `ReactiveFormsModule` and `NumberValueAccessor` are `@publicApi` with no class
265	    deprecation.
266	  - CHANGELOG `forms` scope between 22.0.0 and 22.3.0: 39 fix, perf or feat entries.
267	  - angular.dev Signal Forms overview (unversioned page, read 2026-11-20): "Signal Forms work
268	    best in new applications built with signals." "If you're working with an existing
269	    application that uses reactive forms, reactive forms remain a solid choice."
270	- **Third-party skill conflict (`CLAUDE.md` §1, §5):** the vendored `signal-forms.md` says
271	  "MUST use Signal Forms" and "Use 0 for numbers, NOT null". This ADR reaches Signal Forms on
272	  its own drivers, not because of the skill. It **departs** from the skill on number fields
273	  (string model, `''` for empty) and does not use the skill's built-in validators for
274	  config-driven rules.
275	- **Related ADRs:** ADR-0001 (routes; the step 1 page at `/:country/datos`), ADR-0003 (the
276	  store that provides `storedValues`, prunes stale keys and options, and receives `toOutput`).
277	- **Revisit when:** a real-browser test or the HC3 pass shows focus, number or date behaviour
278	  that Signal Forms cannot meet; an Angular upgrade (which needs its own ADR, `CLAUDE.md` §4)
279	  changes a Signal Forms API we use; or a later story needs dynamic form features (arrays,
280	  cross-field rules) that the spike did not cover.

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

689	### 7.4 Differences from the `dynamic-form-fields` skill contract v0

691	The skill says the US-01 spec may refine the contract and that the skill is updated in the same

701	## 8. UI states

703	| State | Trigger | What the user sees | Accessibility notes |
704	|---|---|---|---|
705	| Loading | Country resolved, configuration request in flight | Step heading and "Cargando formulario…"; no fields, no "Continuar" | Container has `aria-busy="true"`; the loading text is in a polite live region |

708	| Partial content | Some fields malformed | The valid fields only; nothing extra is shown to the user | Console warning only (no user data) |
709	| Ready (pristine) | Configuration loaded | Fields in sortOrder, help texts, required marker note, "Continuar" | Label bound to every control; help text in `aria-describedby`; required exposed |

715	## 9. Non-functional requirements

717	- **Accessibility (Assessment):** the step can be completed with the keyboard only (AC-24), and
718	  every field has an accessible label (AC-25). Native controls are used (`input` of type text,

720	  field and announced once. Target: WCAG 2.2 AA for step 1 (verified in part automatically and in
721	  part by hand at HC3, including one screen reader pass).

723	  verified by hand at HC3 at 360 × 740 and 1280 × 800, with screenshots as evidence (AC-26); one
724	  column; touch targets at least 24 × 24 CSS px.

Reserved keys (US-01-Q-08, §7.3): `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
`birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.


### 7.3 Step 1 output (consumed by US-02 and US-03 through the wizard state)

- `country`: `'CO' | 'CL'`.
- `values`: a map from field `key` to value. `text` → trimmed string; `number` → integer;
  `select` → option `value`; `date` → ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string; `checkbox` → boolean. An empty
  optional field → `null`.
- The field configuration used to render the step (labels and option labels), so later steps can
  display values without refetching or hard-coding labels. Whether it is stored or refetched is a
  persistence ADR detail.
- Reserved keys (US-01-Q-08): `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
  `birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.

### 7.4 Differences from the `dynamic-form-fields` skill contract v0

The skill says the US-01 spec may refine the contract and that the skill is updated in the same
PR. Differences proposed here:

1. A required field-level `errorMessage` plus optional per-rule overrides (`requiredMessage`,
   rule `message`), instead of only a per-rule-kind `messages` map (US-01-Q-04).
2. A new rule kind `rutCheckDigit` (US-01-Q-09).
3. `number` fields are integers only (US-01-Q-12).
4. Empty optional fields skip all rules (US-01-Q-26). The skill does not state this.
5. Rules carry an applicability by field type (§7.1); a mismatch is malformed.

## 8. UI states

| State | Trigger | What the user sees | Accessibility notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Loading | Country resolved, configuration request in flight | Step heading and "Cargando formulario…"; no fields, no "Continuar" | Container has `aria-busy="true"`; the loading text is in a polite live region |
| Unsupported country | Missing or unsupported country (US-01-Q-01) | "Este país no está disponible." and links "Colombia", "Chile" | Message is the page's main heading; links are reachable by Tab |
| Error | Timeout (10 s), network or HTTP error, or zero valid fields | "No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de nuevo." and "Reintentar" | Message in `role="alert"`; focus moves to "Reintentar" |
| Partial content | Some fields malformed | The valid fields only; nothing extra is shown to the user | Console warning only (no user data) |
| Ready (pristine) | Configuration loaded | Fields in sortOrder, help texts, required marker note, "Continuar" | Label bound to every control; help text in `aria-describedby`; required exposed |
| Field invalid | Blur or failed "Continuar" | Configured message right below the field | `aria-invalid="true"`; error in `aria-describedby`; announced once |
| Failed continue | "Continuar" with invalid fields | All errors shown; step does not change | Focus on the first invalid field in sortOrder |
| Success | "Continuar" with a valid form | The address changes to the step 2 route; its page is US-02's (no page of its own in US-01, US-01-Q-27) | Focus on the step 2 heading and document title: defined and verified in US-02 |
| Back to step 1 | Browser back (and "Atrás" on step 2, once US-02 exists) | Step 1 with the stored values, no errors | Focus on the step 1 heading |

## 9. Non-functional requirements

- **Accessibility (Assessment):** the step can be completed with the keyboard only (AC-24), and
  every field has an accessible label (AC-25). Native controls are used (`input` of type text,
  number, date and checkbox; `select`). Visible focus indicator. Errors are associated with their
  field and announced once. Target: WCAG 2.2 AA for step 1 (verified in part automatically and in
  part by hand at HC3, including one screen reader pass).
- **Responsive (Assessment):** usable from 320 to 1440 CSS px wide without horizontal scroll;
  verified by hand at HC3 at 360 × 740 and 1280 × 800, with screenshots as evidence (AC-26); one
  column; touch targets at least 24 × 24 CSS px.
- **Multi-country (Assessment):** one build for CO and CL; no country-specific code paths for
  fields or copy (BR-07).
- **Content-driven (Assessment, BR-06):** every field-related string, option, rule and the order
  come from Strapi. No field list is hard-coded in the front end.
- **Typed validations (Assessment):** the configuration is parsed at the boundary into a typed
  model (§7.1) before it reaches the form; validators are pure functions with an injectable clock.
- **Security / privacy (Assessment, CLAUDE.md §3):** no Strapi token with write permissions
  reaches the browser; the browser only reads content (AC-27). Public role permissions are
  minimal and justified in the security ADR. Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written
  to logs; console warnings contain no user data. Seed and test data are fictitious.
- **Performance:** the configuration of a country is loaded with as few requests as the content
  model allows (target: one), with options and rules populated in the same response. No request
  per keystroke. Validation runs on the client.
- **Environment (Assessment):** the stack starts with a single command (for example
  `docker compose up`) with the seed for both countries.
- **Language:** all end-user copy is Spanish; code, logs and docs are English.

## 10. ADRs

- **Referenced (accepted):** none yet.
- **Needed (for the architect):**
  1. **Multi-country content strategy:** the Strapi model for country-specific fields (options
     A–D in `strapi-content-modeling`), where country metadata lives, and how Angular resolves
     the country context, including the root address, unsupported countries and switching.
     Inputs: BR-07, US-01-Q-01, US-01-Q-02, §7. Shared with US-02 and US-03.
  2. **Forms library (SPIKE-01):** Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms for a form built at runtime
     from §7.1. Beyond the cases already listed in CLAUDE.md §7 (required number, empty date,
     select, legal age), the spike should also cover: hydrating the form from the wizard state
     (AC-04), dropping stored values for removed fields (AC-23), error display timing and focusing
     the first invalid field (AC-10), and integer-only numbers (AC-05). This spec is
     library-agnostic.
  3. **Strapi access and security model:** public role (`find` only) vs. a read-only token
     behind a server-side proxy; runtime configuration of the API URL so the same build serves
     every environment; no caching that breaks BR-06 (US-01-Q-16); how e2e tests write test
     content without exposing write tokens to the browser (US-01-Q-23). Inputs: AC-27, AC-03.
  4. **Front-end persistence of wizard state:** in-memory vs `sessionStorage` vs `localStorage`;
     what is stored (personal data included), scoping per country, and when it is cleared
     (country switch, tab close, after payment in US-03). Inputs: BR-08, US-01-Q-02,
     US-01-Q-15, AC-04, AC-20, AC-21, AC-22.
  - Candidate for the architect to fold into ADR 1 or write separately: **wizard routing and
    step guards** (step URLs, history entries per step, guard rule of US-01-Q-19, focus
    management on step change). Shared by all three stories. Since v0.2 it also covers how the
    step 2 route exists before its page (US-01-Q-27).

Planned locations follow CLAUDE.md §6; the test-engineer may adjust the unit and component paths
once the ADRs fix the structure. "HC3" notes are extra human checks, not a replacement for the
automated test.

1	# SPIKE-01: Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms for the Strapi-driven step 1 form
2	
3	| Item | Value |
4	|---|---|
5	| Question | Which forms library fits a step 1 form built at runtime from the Strapi field configuration (`CLAUDE.md` §7, spec §10 item 2)? |
6	| Run by | frontend-developer subagent (Claude Opus 5.5), 2026-11-20 |
7	| Independent re-run | orchestrator, 2026-11-20: `@angular/core` and `@angular/forms` 22.3.0 installed, `ng build` OK, `ng test` 4 files, 38/38 passed |
8	| Written up by | architect subagent (Claude Opus 5.5), 2026-11-20 |
9	| Code | Branch `spike/01-forms`, commit `be9ae50`, folder `spikes/spike-01-forms/` (throwaway, **never merged**). GitHub: <https://github.com/FelipeSuarez25/multicountry-car-insurance/tree/spike/01-forms/spikes/spike-01-forms> |
10	| Decision informed | [ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-forms-library.md) (forms library) |
11	
12	This document records facts only. The recommendation is in ADR-0004.
13	
14	## Environment
15	
16	| Item | Version or setting |
17	|---|---|
18	| Node | 24.22.1 |
19	| Scaffold | `npx @angular/cli@22.3.0 new spike-01-forms --directory spikes/spike-01-forms --skip-git --ssr=false --style=css --skip-install --defaults` |
20	| `@angular/core` / `forms` / `common` | 22.3.0 (checked in `node_modules`) |
21	| TypeScript | 6.0.3 |
22	| Vitest | 5.1.1 (through `ng test`, `@angular/build:unit-test`) |
23	| DOM | jsdom 31 (**no real browser**) |
24	| tsconfig | The CLI default has no `strict`; the spike adds `strict: true` and `resolveJsonModule: true`. `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off. |
25	| Change detection | zoneless (CLI default) |
26	
27	Environment notes: `ng build` hung silently on an interactive analytics prompt until
28	`NG_CLI_ANALYTICS=false CI=1` were set. `npm install` printed install-script warnings (esbuild,
29	lmdb, msgpackr-extract); build and tests were not affected. The spike `package.json` uses `^`
30	ranges, which is acceptable for a throwaway spike only (`CLAUDE.md` §4 applies to `frontend/`).
31	
32	## Method
33	
34	- One fixture JSON that follows the `dynamic-form-fields` contract v1 (57 lines), parsed at the
35	  boundary into typed `FieldConfig` objects.
36	- A **shared, library-agnostic core** (`src/app/core/`, 209 lines): pure functions with no
37	  Angular import except the `CLOCK` token (`InjectionToken<() => Date>`): `parseFieldConfigs`,
38	  `validateField(cfg, value, today)` (required, then empty-optional skip, then integer-only,
39	  then rules in configuration order; the first failing message wins), `hydrate`, `toOutput`,
40	  `parseIsoDate`, `ageOn`. `rutCheckDigit` is not implemented.
41	- Two adapters with the same inputs, output and test handles: Signal Forms
42	  (`signal-forms/dynamic-form-signal.*`, 111 lines) and Reactive Forms with `FormRecord`
43	  (`reactive-forms/dynamic-form-reactive.*`, 112 lines). Each field gets **one custom
44	  validator** that calls `validateField`. Built-in validators (`required()`, `min()`,
45	  `pattern()`, `Validators.*`) were not used.
46	- Tests (435 lines): `criteria.spec.ts` runs the same titled test against both adapters
47	  (`[signal-forms] (x)` / `[reactive-forms] (x)`); `core.spec.ts` covers the core once;
48	  `typing.spec.ts` covers compile-time behaviour; `library-facts.spec.ts` isolates library
49	  behaviour outside the shared criteria.
50	- API facts were read from the installed `@angular/forms` typings (`types/signals.d.ts`,
51	  `types/_structure-chunk.d.ts`) and compiled `fesm2022/*.mjs`.
52	- Sensitivity check: removing `focusBoundControl()` failed `[signal-forms] (i)`; removing
53	  `markAllAsTouched()` failed `[reactive-forms] (h)`. Both were restored.
54	
55	## Results by criterion
56	
57	| # | Criterion (source) | Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) | Reactive Forms (`FormRecord`) |
58	|---|---|---|---|
59	| a | Required number: empty vs `0` vs value; integer-only (`CLAUDE.md` §7, AC-05, AC-08) | **Works.** Model holds a **string** (`''` = empty); a string model on `<input type="number">` falls through to `element.value`. With a `number` model, clearing the input writes `null` and `2020.5` reaches the model, so integer-only is a validator, not a type. | **Works with a workaround.** `NumberValueAccessor` writes `number \| null` even into a `FormControl<string \| boolean>`; numeric `2020` was treated as empty until a `normalise()` step was added (validator input and output mapping). `nonNullable: true` does not stop the accessor writing `null`. Forcing `DefaultValueAccessor` was not tried. |
60	| b | Empty date, required vs optional; empty optional skips `minAge` (AC-06, AC-08) | **Works.** ISO string or `''`; string model on `type=date` falls through to `element.value`. | **Works**, same behaviour (`DefaultValueAccessor` handles `type=date` as a string). |
61	| c | Select required, nothing pre-selected (AC-07, BR-02) | **Works.** Model `''` plus placeholder `<option value="">`; `selectedIndex === 0`; options in `sortOrder`. | **Works**, same. |
62	| d | Legal age with an injectable clock (AC-06) | **Works.** `CLOCK` provided in TestBed; 18th birthday today valid, tomorrow invalid (today 2026-11-20). 29 February covered in `core.spec.ts`. | **Works**, same. |
63	| e | Typing with a runtime-built model (assessment: "typed validations") | Static model: precise keys and types. Runtime `Record<string, string \| boolean>`: any key compiles; an unknown key throws `TypeError` at runtime. The union **does not compile** against native controls, so two cast helpers were needed (see *Typing*). | Static `FormGroup`: precise. `FormRecord<FormControl<string \| boolean>>`: `controls[key]` typed (runtime `undefined` for an unknown key), `get(key)` nullable, `getRawValue()` → `Record<string, string \| boolean>`. `[formControl]` accepts the union **with no cast**. The runtime number value is `number \| null` despite the declared type. |
64	| f | Hydration from stored values (AC-04, AC-21) | **Works.** Model built from `hydrate(configs, stored)` before `form()`; `2020` → `'2020'`; pristine, untouched, no errors on entry; DOM shows input, select and checkbox values. A stored select value that is no longer an option keeps its model value, the select shows the placeholder, and the form is invalid. | **Works**, same results. |
65	| g | Drop stored values of keys no longer configured (AC-23) | **Works only because `hydrate()` filters by configuration before the model exists.** The model signal is the source of truth: an extra key written into it stays in `form().value()`. | **Works** through the same `hydrate()`. `FormGroup.setValue` with an extra key **throws**; `patchValue` ignores it. |
66	| h | When errors become visible (AC-10) | `submit()` marks the root as touched, which propagates to every field, so one condition `touched() && invalid()` covers blur and failed submit. Typing alone does not touch. After a failed submit: 3 alerts (birthDate, make, vehicleYear); optional fields stay quiet. | Needs an explicit `record.markAllAsTouched()` in the submit handler (removing it fails the test). `touched` is a plain property, not a signal; re-render worked because blur and `ngSubmit` are template listeners (zoneless). 67	| i | Focus on the first invalid field after a failed submit (AC-10) | **Works with a built-in API**: `onInvalid` → `root[key]().focusBoundControl()` on the first invalid field in `sortOrder`. `document.activeElement` checked across 3 consecutive attempts. | **No focus API on controls.** Workaround: `host.querySelector('#' + key).focus()` (id = key). 68	| j | Output maps empty optional to `null` while the model stays non-null (§7.3, `CLAUDE.md` §7) | **Works.** Model `Record<string, string \| boolean>` (`''` / `false`); `toOutput()` produces `null`, integers and trimmed text; the model keeps what was typed (`'   '` stays in the model, output is `null`). | **Works** with the same `toOutput()`, after the `normalise()` workaround from (a). |
69	
70	Totals: `[signal-forms]` a–j 11/11, `[reactive-forms]` a–j 11/11, core 8/8, typing 4/4, library
71	facts 4/4; 38/38 overall. `ng build` succeeds.
72	
73	Checkbox note: an unchecked optional checkbox is output as `false`, not `null` (see unverified
74	item 5).
75	
76	## Typing observations
77	
78	- **Signal Forms, static model** (`signal({ vehicleYear: '', acceptsOffers: false })`):
79	  `f.vehicleYear().value()` is `string`; `f.nope` and `.value.set(2020)` are compile errors.
80	- **Signal Forms, runtime model** (`signal<Record<string, string | boolean>>`): `f['anything']`
81	  compiles as `FieldTree<string | boolean>`; an unknown key throws
82	  `TypeError: f.<key> is not a function` at runtime.
83	- **Signal Forms, binding the union in a template does not compile.** Captured `ng build` errors:
84	  text → `TS2322: Type 'WritableSignal<RawValue>' is not assignable to type '{ (): string; set: (v: string) => void; } | { (): number | null; set: (v: number | null) => void; }'`;
85	  checkbox → `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'boolean'`; number →
86	  `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'string | number | null'`; date →
87	  `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'string | number | Date | null'`.
88	  `FieldTree<string | boolean>` is not assignable to `FieldTree<string>`. Workaround: `str(key)`
89	  and `bool(key)` accessors doing `as unknown as FieldTree<string>` / `FieldTree<boolean>`
90	  (2 casts, chosen per field type in a static `@switch`).
91	- Value types accepted by native controls in Signal Forms: text → `string`; number →
92	  `string | number | null`; date → `string | number | Date | null`; checkbox → `boolean`.
93	- **Reactive Forms**, `FormRecord<FormControl<string | boolean>>`: `controls[key]` is
94	  `FormControl<string | boolean>` (no `undefined` because `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off);
95	  `get(key)` is nullable; `setValue(5)` is a compile error; `[formControl]` compiles with no cast.
96	- **Both:** the types describe the model, not what native controls write at runtime (`null` from
97	  a cleared number input).
98	- `form()` inside `computed()` throws `NG0602: effect() cannot be called from within a reactive
99	  context`, because `form()` creates an effect. The adapter wraps it in
100	  `untracked(() => form(...))`. `form()` also needs an injection context or `{ injector }`.
101	  Building a `FormRecord` inside `computed()` had no such issue.
102	
103	## Gotchas found
104	
105	1. A cleared `<input type="number">` writes `null` into a `number` model (Signal Forms) or a
106	   `nonNullable` control (Reactive Forms). Declared types do not protect against it.
107	2. Decimals reach the model in both libraries; integer-only must be a validator.
108	3. Reactive Forms: `NumberValueAccessor` overrides the declared control type, which produced a
109	   real functional bug in the spike (a valid year read as empty) until `normalise()` was added.
110	4. Signal Forms: the model is the source of truth and does not drop unknown keys; filtering by
111	   configuration must happen before the model is built.
112	5. Signal Forms: `form()` cannot be called inside `computed()` without `untracked`.
113	6. Reactive Forms: a failed submit does not touch the controls unless `markAllAsTouched()` is
114	   called; there is no control-level focus API.
115	7. Both: a configuration change while mounted rebuilds the form from `stored`; values typed since
116	   mount are lost unless the caller keeps `stored` current.
117	8. Tooling: `ng build` needs `NG_CLI_ANALYTICS=false CI=1` in a non-interactive shell.
118	
119	## Not verified (open)
120	
121	1. Everything ran in jsdom. Not checked in a real browser: focus and scroll behaviour, native
122	   `date` and `number` UI, `badInput` handling (`NativeInputParseError` exists in the source but
123	   was not exercised), mobile keyboards, screen reader announcement of `role="alert"`.
124	2. Blur was simulated with `new FocusEvent('blur')` and typing with `input`/`change` events; real
125	   event ordering was not covered.
126	3. Reactive Forms with a string model through `DefaultValueAccessor` (for example
127	   `type="text" inputmode="numeric"` or a custom accessor) was not tried.
128	4. `rutCheckDigit` was not implemented.
129	5. Output of an unchecked optional checkbox: `false` in the spike. Spec §7.3 says both
130	   "checkbox → boolean" and "empty optional field → `null`".
131	6. Whether step 1 can receive a different configuration while mounted (country switch) is a spec
132	   and routing question.
133	7. Async validators and `submit({ ignoreValidators })` were not exercised.
134	8. A dynamic `[type]` binding together with `[formField]` was avoided (static `@switch`
135	   branches), so it is unverified.
136	9. Bundle size, performance with many fields and SSR were not measured.
137	10. Error visibility is hand-built in both (`touched && invalid`); `provideSignalFormsConfig`
138	    (class and ARIA auto-binding) was not explored.
139	11. The vendored `signal-forms.md` forbids `null` in the model; the spike confirms that a non-null
140	    model with `null` only in the mapped output works, but also that `null` can still appear at
141	    runtime in a `number` model through native inputs (row a).
142	12. A third approach, binding native inputs to plain signals with no forms library, was not
143	    built. ADR-0004 weighs it from the shared-core evidence only.
