# SPIKE-01: Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms for the Strapi-driven step 1 form

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Question | Which forms library fits a step 1 form built at runtime from the Strapi field configuration (`CLAUDE.md` §7, spec §10 item 2)? |
| Run by | frontend-developer subagent (Claude Opus 5.5), 2026-11-20 |
| Independent re-run | orchestrator, 2026-11-20: `@angular/core` and `@angular/forms` 22.3.0 installed, `ng build` OK, `ng test` 4 files, 38/38 passed |
| Written up by | architect subagent (Claude Opus 5.5), 2026-11-20 |
| Code | Branch `spike/01-forms`, commit `be9ae50`, folder `spikes/spike-01-forms/` (throwaway, **never merged**). GitHub: <https://github.com/FelipeSuarez25/multicountry-car-insurance/tree/spike/01-forms/spikes/spike-01-forms> |
| Decision informed | [ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-forms-library.md) (forms library) |

This document records facts only. The recommendation is in ADR-0004.

## Environment

| Item | Version or setting |
|---|---|
| Node | 24.22.1 |
| Scaffold | `npx @angular/cli@22.3.0 new spike-01-forms --directory spikes/spike-01-forms --skip-git --ssr=false --style=css --skip-install --defaults` |
| `@angular/core` / `forms` / `common` | 22.3.0 (checked in `node_modules`) |
| TypeScript | 6.0.3 |
| Vitest | 5.1.1 (through `ng test`, `@angular/build:unit-test`) |
| DOM | jsdom 31 (**no real browser**) |
| tsconfig | The CLI default has no `strict`; the spike adds `strict: true` and `resolveJsonModule: true`. `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off. |
| Change detection | zoneless (CLI default) |

Environment notes: `ng build` hung silently on an interactive analytics prompt until
`NG_CLI_ANALYTICS=false CI=1` were set. `npm install` printed install-script warnings (esbuild,
lmdb, msgpackr-extract); build and tests were not affected. The spike `package.json` uses `^`
ranges, which is acceptable for a throwaway spike only (`CLAUDE.md` §4 applies to `frontend/`).

## Method

- One fixture JSON that follows the `dynamic-form-fields` contract v1 (57 lines), parsed at the
  boundary into typed `FieldConfig` objects.
- A **shared, library-agnostic core** (`src/app/core/`, 209 lines): pure functions with no
  Angular import except the `CLOCK` token (`InjectionToken<() => Date>`): `parseFieldConfigs`,
  `validateField(cfg, value, today)` (required, then empty-optional skip, then integer-only,
  then rules in configuration order; the first failing message wins), `hydrate`, `toOutput`,
  `parseIsoDate`, `ageOn`. `rutCheckDigit` is not implemented.
- Two adapters with the same inputs, output and test handles: Signal Forms
  (`signal-forms/dynamic-form-signal.*`, 111 lines) and Reactive Forms with `FormRecord`
  (`reactive-forms/dynamic-form-reactive.*`, 112 lines). Each field gets **one custom
  validator** that calls `validateField`. Built-in validators (`required()`, `min()`,
  `pattern()`, `Validators.*`) were not used.
- Tests (435 lines): `criteria.spec.ts` runs the same titled test against both adapters
  (`[signal-forms] (x)` / `[reactive-forms] (x)`); `core.spec.ts` covers the core once;
  `typing.spec.ts` covers compile-time behaviour; `library-facts.spec.ts` isolates library
  behaviour outside the shared criteria.
- API facts were read from the installed `@angular/forms` typings (`types/signals.d.ts`,
  `types/_structure-chunk.d.ts`) and compiled `fesm2022/*.mjs`.
- Sensitivity check: removing `focusBoundControl()` failed `[signal-forms] (i)`; removing
  `markAllAsTouched()` failed `[reactive-forms] (h)`. Both were restored.

## Results by criterion

| # | Criterion (source) | Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) | Reactive Forms (`FormRecord`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| a | Required number: empty vs `0` vs value; integer-only (`CLAUDE.md` §7, AC-05, AC-08) | **Works.** Model holds a **string** (`''` = empty); a string model on `<input type="number">` falls through to `element.value`. With a `number` model, clearing the input writes `null` and `2020.5` reaches the model, so integer-only is a validator, not a type. | **Works with a workaround.** `NumberValueAccessor` writes `number \| null` even into a `FormControl<string \| boolean>`; numeric `2020` was treated as empty until a `normalise()` step was added (validator input and output mapping). `nonNullable: true` does not stop the accessor writing `null`. Forcing `DefaultValueAccessor` was not tried. |
| b | Empty date, required vs optional; empty optional skips `minAge` (AC-06, AC-08) | **Works.** ISO string or `''`; string model on `type=date` falls through to `element.value`. | **Works**, same behaviour (`DefaultValueAccessor` handles `type=date` as a string). |
| c | Select required, nothing pre-selected (AC-07, BR-02) | **Works.** Model `''` plus placeholder `<option value="">`; `selectedIndex === 0`; options in `sortOrder`. | **Works**, same. |
| d | Legal age with an injectable clock (AC-06) | **Works.** `CLOCK` provided in TestBed; 18th birthday today valid, tomorrow invalid (today 2026-11-20). 29 February covered in `core.spec.ts`. | **Works**, same. |
| e | Typing with a runtime-built model (assessment: "typed validations") | Static model: precise keys and types. Runtime `Record<string, string \| boolean>`: any key compiles; an unknown key throws `TypeError` at runtime. The union **does not compile** against native controls, so two cast helpers were needed (see *Typing*). | Static `FormGroup`: precise. `FormRecord<FormControl<string \| boolean>>`: `controls[key]` typed (runtime `undefined` for an unknown key), `get(key)` nullable, `getRawValue()` → `Record<string, string \| boolean>`. `[formControl]` accepts the union **with no cast**. The runtime number value is `number \| null` despite the declared type. |
| f | Hydration from stored values (AC-04, AC-21) | **Works.** Model built from `hydrate(configs, stored)` before `form()`; `2020` → `'2020'`; pristine, untouched, no errors on entry; DOM shows input, select and checkbox values. A stored select value that is no longer an option keeps its model value, the select shows the placeholder, and the form is invalid. | **Works**, same results. |
| g | Drop stored values of keys no longer configured (AC-23) | **Works only because `hydrate()` filters by configuration before the model exists.** The model signal is the source of truth: an extra key written into it stays in `form().value()`. | **Works** through the same `hydrate()`. `FormGroup.setValue` with an extra key **throws**; `patchValue` ignores it. |
| h | When errors become visible (AC-10) | `submit()` marks the root as touched, which propagates to every field, so one condition `touched() && invalid()` covers blur and failed submit. Typing alone does not touch. After a failed submit: 3 alerts (birthDate, make, vehicleYear); optional fields stay quiet. | Needs an explicit `record.markAllAsTouched()` in the submit handler (removing it fails the test). `touched` is a plain property, not a signal; re-render worked because blur and `ngSubmit` are template listeners (zoneless). Same visible behaviour. |
| i | Focus on the first invalid field after a failed submit (AC-10) | **Works with a built-in API**: `onInvalid` → `root[key]().focusBoundControl()` on the first invalid field in `sortOrder`. `document.activeElement` checked across 3 consecutive attempts. | **No focus API on controls.** Workaround: `host.querySelector('#' + key).focus()` (id = key). Same result. |
| j | Output maps empty optional to `null` while the model stays non-null (§7.3, `CLAUDE.md` §7) | **Works.** Model `Record<string, string \| boolean>` (`''` / `false`); `toOutput()` produces `null`, integers and trimmed text; the model keeps what was typed (`'   '` stays in the model, output is `null`). | **Works** with the same `toOutput()`, after the `normalise()` workaround from (a). |

Totals: `[signal-forms]` a–j 11/11, `[reactive-forms]` a–j 11/11, core 8/8, typing 4/4, library
facts 4/4; 38/38 overall. `ng build` succeeds.

Checkbox note: an unchecked optional checkbox is output as `false`, not `null` (see unverified
item 5).

## Typing observations

- **Signal Forms, static model** (`signal({ vehicleYear: '', acceptsOffers: false })`):
  `f.vehicleYear().value()` is `string`; `f.nope` and `.value.set(2020)` are compile errors.
- **Signal Forms, runtime model** (`signal<Record<string, string | boolean>>`): `f['anything']`
  compiles as `FieldTree<string | boolean>`; an unknown key throws
  `TypeError: f.<key> is not a function` at runtime.
- **Signal Forms, binding the union in a template does not compile.** Captured `ng build` errors:
  text → `TS2322: Type 'WritableSignal<RawValue>' is not assignable to type '{ (): string; set: (v: string) => void; } | { (): number | null; set: (v: number | null) => void; }'`;
  checkbox → `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'boolean'`; number →
  `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'string | number | null'`; date →
  `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'string | number | Date | null'`.
  `FieldTree<string | boolean>` is not assignable to `FieldTree<string>`. Workaround: `str(key)`
  and `bool(key)` accessors doing `as unknown as FieldTree<string>` / `FieldTree<boolean>`
  (2 casts, chosen per field type in a static `@switch`).
- Value types accepted by native controls in Signal Forms: text → `string`; number →
  `string | number | null`; date → `string | number | Date | null`; checkbox → `boolean`.
- **Reactive Forms**, `FormRecord<FormControl<string | boolean>>`: `controls[key]` is
  `FormControl<string | boolean>` (no `undefined` because `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off);
  `get(key)` is nullable; `setValue(5)` is a compile error; `[formControl]` compiles with no cast.
- **Both:** the types describe the model, not what native controls write at runtime (`null` from
  a cleared number input).
- `form()` inside `computed()` throws `NG0602: effect() cannot be called from within a reactive
  context`, because `form()` creates an effect. The adapter wraps it in
  `untracked(() => form(...))`. `form()` also needs an injection context or `{ injector }`.
  Building a `FormRecord` inside `computed()` had no such issue.

## Gotchas found

1. A cleared `<input type="number">` writes `null` into a `number` model (Signal Forms) or a
   `nonNullable` control (Reactive Forms). Declared types do not protect against it.
2. Decimals reach the model in both libraries; integer-only must be a validator.
3. Reactive Forms: `NumberValueAccessor` overrides the declared control type, which produced a
   real functional bug in the spike (a valid year read as empty) until `normalise()` was added.
4. Signal Forms: the model is the source of truth and does not drop unknown keys; filtering by
   configuration must happen before the model is built.
5. Signal Forms: `form()` cannot be called inside `computed()` without `untracked`.
6. Reactive Forms: a failed submit does not touch the controls unless `markAllAsTouched()` is
   called; there is no control-level focus API.
7. Both: a configuration change while mounted rebuilds the form from `stored`; values typed since
   mount are lost unless the caller keeps `stored` current.
8. Tooling: `ng build` needs `NG_CLI_ANALYTICS=false CI=1` in a non-interactive shell.

## Not verified (open)

1. Everything ran in jsdom. Not checked in a real browser: focus and scroll behaviour, native
   `date` and `number` UI, `badInput` handling (`NativeInputParseError` exists in the source but
   was not exercised), mobile keyboards, screen reader announcement of `role="alert"`.
2. Blur was simulated with `new FocusEvent('blur')` and typing with `input`/`change` events; real
   event ordering was not covered.
3. Reactive Forms with a string model through `DefaultValueAccessor` (for example
   `type="text" inputmode="numeric"` or a custom accessor) was not tried.
4. `rutCheckDigit` was not implemented.
5. Output of an unchecked optional checkbox: `false` in the spike. Spec §7.3 says both
   "checkbox → boolean" and "empty optional field → `null`".
6. Whether step 1 can receive a different configuration while mounted (country switch) is a spec
   and routing question.
7. Async validators and `submit({ ignoreValidators })` were not exercised.
8. A dynamic `[type]` binding together with `[formField]` was avoided (static `@switch`
   branches), so it is unverified.
9. Bundle size, performance with many fields and SSR were not measured.
10. Error visibility is hand-built in both (`touched && invalid`); `provideSignalFormsConfig`
    (class and ARIA auto-binding) was not explored.
11. The vendored `signal-forms.md` forbids `null` in the model; the spike confirms that a non-null
    model with `null` only in the mapped output works, but also that `null` can still appear at
    runtime in a `number` model through native inputs (row a).
12. A third approach, binding native inputs to plain signals with no forms library, was not
    built. ADR-0004 weighs it from the shared-core evidence only.

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	Global context for every agent working in this repository (main session and subagents).
4	The rules here are binding. If a rule seems wrong, stop and ask the human; do not work around it.
5	
6	Related files: [FLOW.md](FLOW.md) (the flow, step by step), [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (catalogue of
7	agents and skills), [README.md](README.md) (how to run the project).
8	
9	## 1. Precedence of instructions
10	
11	An explicit instruction from the human in the session overrides everything below, and it must be
12	**recorded** where it applies (spec Review log, ADR, or `tasks.md`) so the decision is traceable.
13	Among the written sources, when two disagree, the higher one wins:
14	
15	1. **`CLAUDE.md`** (this file)
16	2. **Accepted ADRs** in `adr/` (status `Accepted`; `Proposed` ADRs are not binding)
17	3. **Project skills**: skills in `.claude/skills/` written for this project
18	4. **Third-party skills**: vendored skills listed in `.claude/skills/THIRD_PARTY.md`
19	
20	A third-party skill never overrides a project decision. If one tells you to do something that a
21	higher source forbids or has not yet decided, follow the higher source and note the conflict in
22	your output.
23	
24	## 2. Language
25	
26	- Everything in the repository is in **English**: code, identifiers, comments, Markdown docs
27	  (README, FLOW, specs, ADRs, reviews), commit messages, branch names, PRs, review comments,
28	  and agent and skill definitions.
29	- **End-user content is in Spanish**: Strapi seed data (labels, help texts, error messages,
30	  plans, coverages, terms and conditions), because the users are in Colombia and Chile.
31	
32	## 3. Security and data
33	
34	- Never print tokens, secrets or the contents of `.env` files in any output.
35	- `.env` is git-ignored. Only `.env.example` with fictitious values is committed.
36	- Only fictitious data anywhere in the repo (people, documents, plates, cards).
37	- No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser.
38	- Do not use skills, plugins or memory from the user's global `~/.claude`. Everything the flow
39	  uses is versioned in this repository.
40	
41	## 4. Toolchain versions (pinned)
42	
43	| Tool | Version | Rule |
44	|---|---|---|
45	| Angular CLI / framework | **22.3.0** (latest stable, verified on npm on 2026-11-20) | Scaffold with `npx @angular/cli@22.3.0 new …`. **Never use `@latest`** or an unpinned `npx @angular/cli`. Pin exact versions in `package.json` (no `^`/`~` on `@angular/*`). |
46	| Unit tests | Vitest (Angular 22 CLI default) | — |
47	| E2E tests | `@playwright/test` | Do not use `playwright-ng-schematics` unless a human approves it. |
48	
49	Upgrading any pinned version requires an ADR or an explicit human approval recorded in the
50	relevant `tasks.md`.
51	
52	## 5. Third-party skill overrides
53	
54	These rules override the vendored `angular-developer` skill (see
55	`docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md`, EVAL-001):
56	
57	- **Forms strategy is not taken from the skill.** `references/signal-forms.md` says Signal Forms
58	  are mandatory; that is not binding. The forms strategy is **ADR-0004** (Accepted 2026-11-20,
59	  after SPIKE-01): Signal Forms over a shared, library-agnostic validation core. Where ADR-0004
60	  differs from the skill (for example, number fields hold strings in the model, not `0`), follow
61	  ADR-0004.
62	- **The Angular CLI MCP server is not used.** Do not configure it (`references/mcp.md`) and do
63	  not run `npx @angular/cli mcp`.
64	- **The Angular CLI version is pinned** (§4). The skill's "no version / `@latest`" defaults do
65	  not apply.
66	- **Naming follows §6**, not the skill's ambiguous examples.
67	- **Keyboard accessibility of the wizard** is enforced by the project `review-checklist` skill.
68	  The skill's ARIA guidance is supplementary.
69	- Reads of `angular.dev` are allowed as a reference, but any decision based on them must be
70	  written into a spec or ADR.
71	- Never edit vendored skill files. Overrides go here.
72	
73	## 6. Naming conventions
74	
75	Status: **Accepted** — approved by Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20.
76	
77	The rule is to follow the Angular 22 CLI defaults (no role suffix in file or class names)
78	and to use **intent-revealing names** so the role stays obvious without a suffix.
79	
80	### Angular (`frontend/`)
81	
82	| Artifact | File | Identifier | Example |
83	|---|---|---|---|
84	| Component | `kebab-case.ts` + `.html` + `.css` (same base name) | `PascalCase`, no `Component` suffix | `plan-list.ts` → `PlanList` |
85	| Routed page (wizard step) | `<step>-page.ts` | `…Page` | `quote-form-page.ts` → `QuoteFormPage` |
86	| Service: HTTP access | `<domain>-api.ts` | `…Api` | `country-content-api.ts` → `CountryContentApi` |
87	| Service: signal state | `<domain>-store.ts` | `…Store` | `quote-store.ts` → `QuoteStore` |
88	| Guard / interceptor / resolver (functions) | `<name>-guard.ts`, `-interceptor.ts`, `-resolver.ts` | `camelCase` + role | `wizard-step-guard.ts` → `wizardStepGuard` |
89	| Pipe | `<name>-pipe.ts` | `…Pipe`; template name `camelCase` | `masked-document-pipe.ts` → `MaskedDocumentPipe` / `maskedDocument` |
90	| Directive | `<name>.ts` | `PascalCase` | `autofocus-error.ts` → `AutofocusError` |
91	| Types / models | `<domain>.model.ts` | `PascalCase` interfaces and types, no `I` prefix | `field-config.model.ts` → `FieldConfig` |
92	| Pure functions | `<domain>.ts` | `camelCase` exported functions | `price-rules.ts` → `calculateFinalPrice()` |
93	| Validators | `<domain>-validators.ts` | `camelCase` factories | `field-validators.ts` → `legalAge()` |
94	| Unit tests | `<same-base-name>.spec.ts` next to the file | `describe('<US-AC id> …')` | `price-rules.spec.ts` |

# CLAUDE.md

Global context for every agent working in this repository (main session and subagents).
The rules here are binding. If a rule seems wrong, stop and ask the human; do not work around it.

Related files: [FLOW.md](FLOW.md) (the flow, step by step), [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (catalogue of
agents and skills), [README.md](README.md) (how to run the project).

## 1. Precedence of instructions

An explicit instruction from the human in the session overrides everything below, and it must be
**recorded** where it applies (spec Review log, ADR, or `tasks.md`) so the decision is traceable.
Among the written sources, when two disagree, the higher one wins:

1. **`CLAUDE.md`** (this file)
2. **Accepted ADRs** in `adr/` (status `Accepted`; `Proposed` ADRs are not binding)
3. **Project skills**: skills in `.claude/skills/` written for this project
4. **Third-party skills**: vendored skills listed in `.claude/skills/THIRD_PARTY.md`

A third-party skill never overrides a project decision. If one tells you to do something that a
higher source forbids or has not yet decided, follow the higher source and note the conflict in
your output.

## 2. Language

- Everything in the repository is in **English**: code, identifiers, comments, Markdown docs
  (README, FLOW, specs, ADRs, reviews), commit messages, branch names, PRs, review comments,
  and agent and skill definitions.
- **End-user content is in Spanish**: Strapi seed data (labels, help texts, error messages,
  plans, coverages, terms and conditions), because the users are in Colombia and Chile.

## 3. Security and data

- Never print tokens, secrets or the contents of `.env` files in any output.
- `.env` is git-ignored. Only `.env.example` with fictitious values is committed.
- Only fictitious data anywhere in the repo (people, documents, plates, cards).
- No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser.
- Do not use skills, plugins or memory from the user's global `~/.claude`. Everything the flow
  uses is versioned in this repository.

## 4. Toolchain versions (pinned)

| Tool | Version | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Angular CLI / framework | **22.3.0** (latest stable, verified on npm on 2026-11-20) | Scaffold with `npx @angular/cli@22.3.0 new …`. **Never use `@latest`** or an unpinned `npx @angular/cli`. Pin exact versions in `package.json` (no `^`/`~` on `@angular/*`). |
| Unit tests | Vitest (Angular 22 CLI default) | — |
| E2E tests | `@playwright/test` | Do not use `playwright-ng-schematics` unless a human approves it. |

Upgrading any pinned version requires an ADR or an explicit human approval recorded in the
relevant `tasks.md`.

## 5. Third-party skill overrides

These rules override the vendored `angular-developer` skill (see
`docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md`, EVAL-001):

- **Forms strategy is not taken from the skill.** `references/signal-forms.md` says Signal Forms
  are mandatory; that is not binding. The forms strategy is **ADR-0004** (Accepted 2026-11-20,
  after SPIKE-01): Signal Forms over a shared, library-agnostic validation core. Where ADR-0004
  differs from the skill (for example, number fields hold strings in the model, not `0`), follow
  ADR-0004.
- **The Angular CLI MCP server is not used.** Do not configure it (`references/mcp.md`) and do
  not run `npx @angular/cli mcp`.
- **The Angular CLI version is pinned** (§4). The skill's "no version / `@latest`" defaults do
  not apply.
- **Naming follows §6**, not the skill's ambiguous examples.
- **Keyboard accessibility of the wizard** is enforced by the project `review-checklist` skill.
  The skill's ARIA guidance is supplementary.
- Reads of `angular.dev` are allowed as a reference, but any decision based on them must be
  written into a spec or ADR.
- Never edit vendored skill files. Overrides go here.

## 6. Naming conventions

Status: **Accepted** — approved by Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20.

The rule is to follow the Angular 22 CLI defaults (no role suffix in file or class names)
and to use **intent-revealing names** so the role stays obvious without a suffix.

### Angular (`frontend/`)

| Artifact | File | Identifier | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Component | `kebab-case.ts` + `.html` + `.css` (same base name) | `PascalCase`, no `Component` suffix | `plan-list.ts` → `PlanList` |
| Routed page (wizard step) | `<step>-page.ts` | `…Page` | `quote-form-page.ts` → `QuoteFormPage` |
| Service: HTTP access | `<domain>-api.ts` | `…Api` | `country-content-api.ts` → `CountryContentApi` |
| Service: signal state | `<domain>-store.ts` | `…Store` | `quote-store.ts` → `QuoteStore` |

| Pipe | `<name>-pipe.ts` | `…Pipe`; template name `camelCase` | `masked-document-pipe.ts` → `MaskedDocumentPipe` / `maskedDocument` |
| Directive | `<name>.ts` | `PascalCase` | `autofocus-error.ts` → `AutofocusError` |
| Types / models | `<domain>.model.ts` | `PascalCase` interfaces and types, no `I` prefix | `field-config.model.ts` → `FieldConfig` |

(wizard steps), `src/app/shared/` (reusable presentational UI, pipes, pure functions).

## 8. Agentic flow (summary — full detail in FLOW.md)

695	   rule `message`), instead of only a per-rule-kind `messages` map (US-01-Q-04).

702	
703	| State | Trigger | What the user sees | Accessibility notes |
704	|---|---|---|---|
705	| Loading | Country resolved, configuration request in flight | Step heading and "Cargando formulario…"; no fields, no "Continuar" | Container has `aria-busy="true"`; the loading text is in a polite live region |

76	## Typing observations
77	
78	- **Signal Forms, static model** (`signal({ vehicleYear: '', acceptsOffers: false })`):
79	  `f.vehicleYear().value()` is `string`; `f.nope` and `.value.set(2020)` are compile errors.
80	- **Signal Forms, runtime model** (`signal<Record<string, string | boolean>>`): `f['anything']`
81	  compiles as `FieldTree<string | boolean>`; an unknown key throws
82	  `TypeError: f.<key> is not a function` at runtime.
83	- **Signal Forms, binding the union in a template does not compile.** Captured `ng build` errors:
84	  text → `TS2322: Type 'WritableSignal<RawValue>' is not assignable to type '{ (): string; set: (v: string) => void; } | { (): number | null; set: (v: number | null) => void; }'`;
85	  checkbox → `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'boolean'`; number →
86	  `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'string | number | null'`; date →
87	  `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'string | number | Date | null'`.
88	  `FieldTree<string | boolean>` is not assignable to `FieldTree<string>`. Workaround: `str(key)`
89	  and `bool(key)` accessors doing `as unknown as FieldTree<string>` / `FieldTree<boolean>`
90	  (2 casts, chosen per field type in a static `@switch`).
91	- Value types accepted by native controls in Signal Forms: text → `string`; number →
92	  `string | number | null`; date → `string | number | Date | null`; checkbox → `boolean`.
93	- **Reactive Forms**, `FormRecord<FormControl<string | boolean>>`: `controls[key]` is
94	  `FormControl<string | boolean>` (no `undefined` because `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off);
95	  `get(key)` is nullable; `setValue(5)` is a compile error; `[formControl]` compiles with no cast.
96	- **Both:** the types describe the model, not what native controls write at runtime (`null` from
97	  a cleared number input).
98	- `form()` inside `computed()` throws `NG0602: effect() cannot be called from within a reactive
99	  context`, because `form()` creates an effect. The adapter wraps it in
100	  `untracked(() => form(...))`. `form()` also needs an injection context or `{ injector }`.
101	  Building a `FormRecord` inside `computed()` had no such issue.
102	
103	## Gotchas found
104	
105	1. A cleared `<input type="number">` writes `null` into a `number` model (Signal Forms) or a
106	   `nonNullable` control (Reactive Forms). Declared types do not protect against it.
107	2. Decimals reach the model in both libraries; integer-only must be a validator.
108	3. Reactive Forms: `NumberValueAccessor` overrides the declared control type, which produced a
109	   real functional bug in the spike (a valid year read as empty) until `normalise()` was added.
110	4. Signal Forms: the model is the source of truth and does not drop unknown keys; filtering by
111	   configuration must happen before the model is built.
112	5. Signal Forms: `form()` cannot be called inside `computed()` without `untracked`.
113	6. Reactive Forms: a failed submit does not touch the controls unless `markAllAsTouched()` is
114	   called; there is no control-level focus API.
115	7. Both: a configuration change while mounted rebuilds the form from `stored`; values typed since
116	   mount are lost unless the caller keeps `stored` current.
117	8. Tooling: `ng build` needs `NG_CLI_ANALYTICS=false CI=1` in a non-interactive shell.

119	## Not verified (open)
120	
121	1. Everything ran in jsdom. Not checked in a real browser: focus and scroll behaviour, native
122	   `date` and `number` UI, `badInput` handling (`NativeInputParseError` exists in the source but
123	   was not exercised), mobile keyboards, screen reader announcement of `role="alert"`.
124	2. Blur was simulated with `new FocusEvent('blur')` and typing with `input`/`change` events; real
125	   event ordering was not covered.
126	3. Reactive Forms with a string model through `DefaultValueAccessor` (for example
127	   `type="text" inputmode="numeric"` or a custom accessor) was not tried.
128	4. `rutCheckDigit` was not implemented.
129	5. Output of an unchecked optional checkbox: `false` in the spike. Spec §7.3 says both
130	   "checkbox → boolean" and "empty optional field → `null`".
131	6. Whether step 1 can receive a different configuration while mounted (country switch) is a spec
132	   and routing question.
133	7. Async validators and `submit({ ignoreValidators })` were not exercised.
134	8. A dynamic `[type]` binding together with `[formField]` was avoided (static `@switch`
135	   branches), so it is unverified.
136	9. Bundle size, performance with many fields and SSR were not measured.
137	10. Error visibility is hand-built in both (`touched && invalid`); `provideSignalFormsConfig`
138	    (class and ARIA auto-binding) was not explored.
139	11. The vendored `signal-forms.md` forbids `null` in the model; the spike confirms that a non-null
140	    model with `null` only in the mapped output works, but also that `null` can still appear at
141	    runtime in a `number` model through native inputs (row a).
142	12. A third approach, binding native inputs to plain signals with no forms library, was not
143	    built. ADR-0004 weighs it from the shared-core evidence only.

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	Global context for every agent working in this repository (main session and subagents).
4	The rules here are binding. If a rule seems wrong, stop and ask the human; do not work around it.
5	
6	Related files: [FLOW.md](FLOW.md) (the flow, step by step), [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (catalogue of
7	agents and skills), [README.md](README.md) (how to run the project).
8	
9	## 1. Precedence of instructions
10	
11	An explicit instruction from the human in the session overrides everything below, and it must be
12	**recorded** where it applies (spec Review log, ADR, or `tasks.md`) so the decision is traceable.
13	Among the written sources, when two disagree, the higher one wins:
14	
15	1. **`CLAUDE.md`** (this file)
16	2. **Accepted ADRs** in `adr/` (status `Accepted`; `Proposed` ADRs are not binding)
17	3. **Project skills**: skills in `.claude/skills/` written for this project
18	4. **Third-party skills**: vendored skills listed in `.claude/skills/THIRD_PARTY.md`
19	
20	A third-party skill never overrides a project decision. If one tells you to do something that a
21	higher source forbids or has not yet decided, follow the higher source and note the conflict in
22	your output.
23	
24	## 2. Language
25	
26	- Everything in the repository is in **English**: code, identifiers, comments, Markdown docs
27	  (README, FLOW, specs, ADRs, reviews), commit messages, branch names, PRs, review comments,
28	  and agent and skill definitions.
29	- **End-user content is in Spanish**: Strapi seed data (labels, help texts, error messages,
30	  plans, coverages, terms and conditions), because the users are in Colombia and Chile.
31	
32	## 3. Security and data
33	
34	- Never print tokens, secrets or the contents of `.env` files in any output.
35	- `.env` is git-ignored. Only `.env.example` with fictitious values is committed.
36	- Only fictitious data anywhere in the repo (people, documents, plates, cards).
37	- No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser.
38	- Do not use skills, plugins or memory from the user's global `~/.claude`. Everything the flow
39	  uses is versioned in this repository.
40	
41	## 4. Toolchain versions (pinned)
42	
43	| Tool | Version | Rule |
44	|---|---|---|
45	| Angular CLI / framework | **22.3.0** (latest stable, verified on npm on 2026-11-20) | Scaffold with `npx @angular/cli@22.3.0 new …`. **Never use `@latest`** or an unpinned `npx @angular/cli`. Pin exact versions in `package.json` (no `^`/`~` on `@angular/*`). |
46	| Unit tests | Vitest (Angular 22 CLI default) | — |
47	| E2E tests | `@playwright/test` | Do not use `playwright-ng-schematics` unless a human approves it. |
48	
49	Upgrading any pinned version requires an ADR or an explicit human approval recorded in the
50	relevant `tasks.md`.
51	
52	## 5. Third-party skill overrides
53	
54	These rules override the vendored `angular-developer` skill (see
55	`docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md`, EVAL-001):
56	
57	- **Forms strategy is not taken from the skill.** `references/signal-forms.md` says Signal Forms
58	  are mandatory; that is not binding. The forms strategy is **ADR-0004** (Accepted 2026-11-20,
59	  after SPIKE-01): Signal Forms over a shared, library-agnostic validation core. Where ADR-0004
60	  differs from the skill (for example, number fields hold strings in the model, not `0`), follow
61	  ADR-0004.
62	- **The Angular CLI MCP server is not used.** Do not configure it (`references/mcp.md`) and do
63	  not run `npx @angular/cli mcp`.
64	- **The Angular CLI version is pinned** (§4). The skill's "no version / `@latest`" defaults do
65	  not apply.
66	- **Naming follows §6**, not the skill's ambiguous examples.
67	- **Keyboard accessibility of the wizard** is enforced by the project `review-checklist` skill.
68	  The skill's ARIA guidance is supplementary.
69	- Reads of `angular.dev` are allowed as a reference, but any decision based on them must be
70	  written into a spec or ADR.
71	- Never edit vendored skill files. Overrides go here.
72	
73	## 6. Naming conventions
74	
75	Status: **Accepted** — approved by Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20.
76	
77	The rule is to follow the Angular 22 CLI defaults (no role suffix in file or class names)
78	and to use **intent-revealing names** so the role stays obvious without a suffix.
79	
80	### Angular (`frontend/`)
81	
82	| Artifact | File | Identifier | Example |
83	|---|---|---|---|
84	| Component | `kebab-case.ts` + `.html` + `.css` (same base name) | `PascalCase`, no `Component` suffix | `plan-list.ts` → `PlanList` |
85	| Routed page (wizard step) | `<step>-page.ts` | `…Page` | `quote-form-page.ts` → `QuoteFormPage` |
86	| Service: HTTP access | `<domain>-api.ts` | `…Api` | `country-content-api.ts` → `CountryContentApi` |
87	| Service: signal state | `<domain>-store.ts` | `…Store` | `quote-store.ts` → `QuoteStore` |
88	| Guard / interceptor / resolver (functions) | `<name>-guard.ts`, `-interceptor.ts`, `-resolver.ts` | `camelCase` + role | `wizard-step-guard.ts` → `wizardStepGuard` |
89	| Pipe | `<name>-pipe.ts` | `…Pipe`; template name `camelCase` | `masked-document-pipe.ts` → `MaskedDocumentPipe` / `maskedDocument` |
90	| Directive | `<name>.ts` | `PascalCase` | `autofocus-error.ts` → `AutofocusError` |
91	| Types / models | `<domain>.model.ts` | `PascalCase` interfaces and types, no `I` prefix | `field-config.model.ts` → `FieldConfig` |
92	| Pure functions | `<domain>.ts` | `camelCase` exported functions | `price-rules.ts` → `calculateFinalPrice()` |
93	| Validators | `<domain>-validators.ts` | `camelCase` factories | `field-validators.ts` → `legalAge()` |
94	| Unit tests | `<same-base-name>.spec.ts` next to the file | `describe('<US-AC id> …')` | `price-rules.spec.ts` |
95	| E2E tests | `frontend/e2e/<us-ids>-<slug>.spec.ts` | `test('<US-AC id> …')` | `us-01-03-full-flow-co.spec.ts` |
96	| Component selector prefix | — | `app-` | `app-plan-card` |
97	| Constants and injection tokens | in the file that owns them | `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` | `STRAPI_BASE_URL` |
98	
99	Folders: `src/app/core/` (singletons, API clients, interceptors), `src/app/features/<feature>/`
100	(wizard steps), `src/app/shared/` (reusable presentational UI, pipes, pure functions).
101	
102	### Strapi (`backend/`)
103	
104	- Content-type API IDs: singular `kebab-case` (`form-field`, `plan`, `country`, `terms`).
105	- Components: `category.kebab-name` (`form.select-option`, `plan.coverage`).
106	- Attribute names: `camelCase` (`isRecommended`, `sortOrder`, `errorMessage`).
107	- Custom code files: `kebab-case.ts`.
108	
109	### Repository artifacts
110	
111	- Specs: `specs/US-01/{story,spec,tasks}.md`
112	- ADRs: `adr/NNNN-kebab-title.md` (4-digit, sequential)
113	- Reviews: `reviews/US-01-review-R1.md`
114	- Branches: `feat/us-01-short-slug`, `fix/us-01-…`, `chore/…`, `docs/…`
115	
116	## 7. Pending decisions
117	
118	| ID | Decision | How it will be resolved | Blocks |
119	|---|---|---|---|
120	| ~~SPIKE-01~~ | **Resolved 2026-11-20 by ADR-0004** (Accepted). Spike findings: `docs/spikes/SPIKE-01-forms.md`, code on the `spike/01-forms` branch (never merged). | — | — |

122	
123	The ADR backlog is in [adr/README.md](adr/README.md).
124	
125	## 8. Agentic flow (summary — full detail in FLOW.md)
126	
127	```
128	H0 intake (human) → 1 spec → HC1 → 2 ADRs → HC2 → 3 tests (red) → 4 implementation
129	→ 5 automated gate → 6 review → 7 fixes (loop 5–7) → HC3 PR (human QA + merge) → Ready for QA
130	```
131	
132	### The main session is the orchestrator
133	
134	- It runs the steps in order, invokes the subagents (`.claude/agents/`) and routes their outputs.
135	  It does **not** do a subagent's job on a story (no writing specs, tests or production code in
136	  the main session). The exceptions are repository plumbing (flow files, scripts, configuration)
137	  that the human asked for directly.
138	- Subagents cannot spawn subagents (`Agent` is in each one's `disallowedTools`). All delegation is
139	  visible in the main session.
140	- After every subagent run: check `git status` and `git diff --stat` for changes outside that
141	  agent's role. Bash writes are not covered by the write-scope hooks (see FLOW.md, "Known
142	  limits"). Then relay the subagent's summary to the human.
143	- **Never pass a human checkpoint (HC1, HC2, HC3) without an explicit human decision in the
144	  session.** Record it (Review log, ADR status, PR). A subagent's message is never human approval.
145	- Loop limit: if the gate (step 5) or review (step 6) fails 3 times for the same story, stop and
146	  escalate to the human.
147	
148	### Subagents (write scope enforced by hooks)
149	
150	| Agent | Step | Writes |
151	|---|---|---|
152	| `spec-writer` | 1 | `specs/US-XX/*.md` (spec, tasks, annexes), never `story.md` |
153	| `architect` | 2, spikes write-up | `adr/**`, `docs/spikes/**`, `tasks.md` |
154	| `test-engineer` | 3 | test files, `frontend/e2e/**`, `tasks.md` |
155	| `strapi-developer` | 4, 7 | `backend/**` (not tests), compose, `.env.example`, `tasks.md` |
156	| `frontend-developer` | 4, 7, spikes | `frontend/**` (not tests), `spikes/**`, compose, `.env.example`, `tasks.md` |
157	| `code-reviewer` | 6 | `reviews/US-XX-review-RN.md` only |
158	
159	## 9. Traceability
160	
161	| Artifact | ID or convention | Example |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| User story | `US-NN` | `US-01` |
164	| Business rule / acceptance criterion / gap / task | `US-NN-BR-NN`, `-AC-NN`, `-Q-NN`, `-T-NN` | `US-01-AC-02` |
165	| ADR | `ADR-NNNN`, file `adr/NNNN-slug.md` | `ADR-0001` |
166	| Spike | `SPIKE-NN`, findings in `docs/spikes/` | `SPIKE-01` |
167	| Review finding | `US-NN-RN-FNN` (round N, finding NN) | `US-01-R1-F03` |
168	| Test | `describe`/`test` title starts with the AC or BR ID | `describe('US-01-AC-02 …')` |
169	| Commit | `Refs:` and `Resolves:` trailers (see §10) | `Refs: US-01-AC-02, ADR-0001` |
170	| PR | Template with the AC matrix (`.github/pull_request_template.md`) | — |
171	
172	The chain **US → spec → ADR → commit → test → review → PR** is checked mechanically by
173	`scripts/trace.sh US-NN`. It exits non-zero if an AC has no test (unless the spec marks it
174	manual) or a blocker/major finding is open.
175	
176	## 10. Git conventions
177	
178	- Branches: see §6 (`feat/us-01-slug`, `spike/01-forms`, `chore/…`, `docs/…`). Spike branches
179	  are never merged.
180	- Commits: [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) in English,
181	  `type(scope): summary`, with trailers:
182	  - `Refs: US-01-AC-02, ADR-0001` (required in `feat`, `fix` and `test` commits of a story)
183	  - `Resolves: US-01-R1-F03` (fix commits for review findings)
184	  - `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` when an agent authored it
185	- Small commits: one task (`US-NN-T-NN`) or one finding per commit where practical. Tests and
186	  production code go in separate commits (they come from different agents).
187	- Local identity only (`git config --local`). The author is the human; agents are co-authors.
188	- No pushes to `main`, no force pushes, and no `--no-verify` (enforced by
189	  `.claude/hooks/guard-bash.mjs`). Changes reach `main` only through a PR merged by the human.
190	
191	## 11. Session continuity
192	
193	Follow the `session-handoff` skill at the start and end of every session. The state of each story
194	lives in `specs/US-NN/tasks.md` (*Current step*, *Next action*). Session logs are exported,
195	unedited, to `logs/sessions/`.
196	
197	## 12. Definition of Done (Ready for QA)
198	
199	A story is **Ready for QA** when all of these hold:
200	
201	- [ ] The spec is `Approved` (HC1), and the ADRs it needs are `Accepted` (HC2).
202	- [ ] Every AC is implemented and has a passing automated test, or a documented manual check.
203	- [ ] Lint, build, unit and e2e pass. `docker compose up` starts the stack with seed data for CO and CL.
204	- [ ] `scripts/trace.sh US-NN` exits 0, and `scripts/scan-secrets.sh` exits 0.
205	- [ ] The last review round is `APPROVED`: no open blocker/major findings; minors are fixed or justified.
206	- [ ] The human did a manual QA pass (both countries, keyboard only, mobile width) and merged the PR (HC3).
207	- [ ] `tasks.md` shows `Ready for QA`, and the session logs are exported.

Note (added in v0.3, HC2 decision, ADR-0004): a `number` input whose text the browser cannot
parse (for example `abc` or `1e`) reaches the form model as empty (`''`), because of the HTML
value sanitisation rule for `<input type="number">`. The field is then handled as empty: a
**required** field fails the `required` check and shows its `requiredMessage` if configured,
otherwise its `errorMessage` (the seed's CO "Modelo (año)" has no `requiredMessage`, so the
field-level message is shown); an **optional** field is treated as empty, so it is valid and
its output is `null` (US-01-Q-26, §7.3). The app does not show a separate "not a number"
message. Unit tests cover the empty-value path; the CO e2e test
(`us-01-data-form-co.spec.ts`) confirms the sanitisation in a real browser, because jsdom does
not reproduce it (SPIKE-01, *Not verified* item 1).

This section is **logical**. The physical model is fixed by ADR-0001 and implemented by the
strapi-developer following `strapi-content-modeling`: a `country` collection type (`code`
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 upper case, unique; `name`; `currencyCode`; `locale`; `sortOrder`; draft &
publish on) and a `form-field` collection type with a **required `manyToOne` relation
`country`**; `documents.strictRelations: true`, so an item without a country cannot be
published; `key` uniqueness per country enforced by a Document Service middleware (Strapi's
`unique` is not scoped by relation). The front end reads one country's fields in one request
filtered by `country.code`, and reads only published content through the same-origin proxy
(ADR-0002).

input.new_string:
Two shapes exist (ADR-0003, HC2 decision). Only the second one is consumed by US-02 and US-03.

**Stored editing values** (written on every change; what a reload restores):

- `country`: the country code of the context (see below).
- `values`: a map from field `key` to the **raw editing value** of the form model, as typed:
  a string for `text`, `number`, `select` and `date`, a boolean for `checkbox`, and `''` for an
  empty field. In-progress invalid values (for example `'2015.5'`) are stored as typed. The model
  never holds `null` (ADR-0004).

**Typed step 1 output** (produced only on a valid "Continuar"; never on an invalid one):

- `country`: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in upper case (`^[A-Z]{2}$`) that matches a published
  `country` entry loaded from Strapi in this page load (ADR-0001). `CO` and `CL` are the seeded
  values; the type is not a fixed union of them.
- `values`: a map from field `key` to value. `text` → trimmed string; `number` → integer;
  `select` → option `value`; `date` → ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string. An empty **optional** `text`,
  `number`, `select` or `date` field → `null`. `checkbox` → always a boolean: checked → `true`,
  unchecked → `false`, also when the checkbox is optional (HC2 decision); a checkbox is never
  `null`.
- The field configuration is **not** stored: later steps read labels and option labels from the
  configuration fetched in the same page load (refetched on every full page load, ADR-0003,
  US-01-Q-16).

  - error: "No pudimos cargar la lista de países. Intenta de nuevo." with the existing "Reintentar"
  - loading: "Cargando…"
  - 10 s timeout, no automatic retries
- The human should confirm or change this copy at HC1 round 3; if left unanswered, the default applies.

**4. ADRs needed:** none. §10 now cites ADR-0001..0004 as accepted and binding, says what each covers, and says "Needed: none".

**Changes, by item**
1. **Country type (ADR-0001):** §7.3 `country` is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code checked against the published `country` entries loaded from Strapi. The glossary, §2 and BR-07 match it. The seed and the examples are unchanged.
2. **Country list could not be loaded (ADR-0001):**
   - §8 has two new states for the root chooser and the unknown-country page: "Country list loading" and "Country list unavailable". The second shows the error with "Reintentar" and never "Este país no está disponible.".
   - The "Unsupported country" state now applies only once the list has loaded.
   - AC-17 now starts from a loaded list, and has a second scenario for a failed list load at `/`, `/ar/datos` and `/co/datos`.
3. **AC-28 (ADR-0002):** it is linked to BR-06 ("drafts never shown"), which fits better than BR-07.
   - Anonymous `status=draft` requests return no seeded `email` field, both on Strapi's own port and through the proxy.
   - `POST /api/form-fields` through the proxy returns 405, and nothing is created (checked by reading key `securityProbe` back anonymously).
   - The e2e test goes in `us-01-security.spec.ts` and runs from the Node process. §11 and BR-06's coverage column are updated.
4. **Tasks:** T-18, T-19 and T-20 are re-scoped. Where one task would have been overloaded I added T-32..T-38 (details in the ID list below). The other tasks now cite ADR numbers.
5. **§11:** AC-17's unit file is now `supported-country-guard.spec.ts`.
6. **Checkbox:** an unchecked optional checkbox gives `false`, never `null`. "Empty optional field → `null`" now applies only to text, number, select and date.
7. **Store shape (ADR-0003):**
   - §7.3 now has two shapes: the stored raw editing values, and the typed output produced only on a valid "Continuar". BR-08 and the glossary match.
   - AC-18 now says "typed step 1 output" and has a new scenario: an invalid "Continuar" produces no typed output.
   - AC-21 now says `sessionStorage` applies, and has a new scenario: an unfinished step 1 (`'2015.5'`) comes back exactly as typed after a reload.
   - AC-23's preamble is updated. AC-20 had no conflict and is unchanged.
8. **AC-09 (ADR-0004):** a new scenario and note. A number the browser cannot parse (`abc`, `1e`) reaches the model as empty: a required field shows `requiredMessage`, else `errorMessage`; an optional field is treated as empty. The CO e2e test confirms it in a real browser by typing `1e` key by key in "Modelo (año)". Because CO "Modelo (año)" has no `requiredMessage`, it shows the field-level message.
9. **ADR references:** cited by number in the metadata, sources, §2, §3, §5, §7, §7.1, §7.3, §9, §10 and §11. The Q rows (Q-01, Q-15, Q-23) still mention "the … ADR" because I left answered rows as they were.

**IDs changed or added**
- BR changed: US-01-BR-06, US-01-BR-07, US-01-BR-08.
- AC changed:
  - Gherkin or notes: US-01-AC-09, US-01-AC-17, US-01-AC-18, US-01-AC-21, US-01-AC-23.
  - §11 mapping only: US-01-AC-09, US-01-AC-17, US-01-AC-18, US-01-AC-21.
- AC added: US-01-AC-28.
- Q added: US-01-Q-28.
- T re-scoped: US-01-T-18, US-01-T-19, US-01-T-20.
- T reworded to cite ADRs or new ACs: T-08, T-09, T-10, T-11 (adds AC-09), T-12, T-13, T-14 (adds AC-28), T-15, T-16, T-17 (adds country seed and AC-17), T-21..T-26. T-01..T-06 status now reads "Accepted at HC2".
- T added:
  - US-01-T-32: dev super admin from env vars; delete the default Full Access token.
  - US-01-T-33: published-only middleware; CORS allow-list.
  - US-01-T-34: `strictRelations` and the key-uniqueness middleware.
  - US-01-T-35: nginx GET-only allow-listed proxy with `no-store`.
  - US-01-T-36: `CountryStore` and its loading/error states.
  - US-01-T-37: `supported-country-guard.spec.ts`.
  - US-01-T-38: backend test of the ADR-0001 Strapi rules.
- Nothing was renumbered or retired.

**Things the orchestrator should know**
- US-01-T-38 goes beyond the list you gave me. ADR-0001 asks for a test of the key-uniqueness middleware, and backend tests belong to the test-engineer, not the strapi-developer.
- In AC-17 and §11, the country list failure is simulated in the e2e test by aborting the `/api/countries` request in the browser context. ADR-0002 only forbids passing tokens into `page.route`, so this is allowed.
